title: Decommission the Fly signet process — sequenced after c784cf, with binding and secret cleanup
description:
Follows the runtime-split decision (signet-1c457e): the edge is the authority, the Fly-hosted Go process goes away. signet-68751f (harden Fly) closed obsolete; this is the removal.

SEQUENCING IS THE WHOLE POINT — do not shut down first. Today /exchange-token and /api/cert/register return 500 because notme's Worker proxies unmatched paths through env.VPC_AUTH to the Fly signet process, and that process cannot start (rig's entrypoint.signet.sh runs /app/signet while rig/docker/Dockerfile installs to /usr/local/bin/signet). That outage is currently a BUG — fixable by one path correction. Killing the app converts it into a permanent removal of two documented CLI commands with no replacement, unless c784cf has already moved those flows to the Worker.

Correct order:
1. signet-c784cf lands — /login + /callback, /exchange-token, /api/cert/register served at the edge.
2. Verify the endpoints live: they should stop returning 500 and start returning real responses, checked against the live authority rather than a staging assumption.
3. Only then remove the Fly app.

Cleanup that outlives the app, and is easy to leave dangling:
- notme: the VPC_AUTH service binding and the unmatched-path fallthrough at worker/worker.ts:2988-2991. A binding to a dead app is a silent 500 generator; removing the app without removing the fallthrough leaves the same symptom with a less discoverable cause.
- rig: the `signet` process group in fly.toml (internal port 8081), entrypoint.signet.sh, and the Dockerfile install path — the last two being the bug that made this urgent.
- Secrets, using the inventory from the closed signet-68751f as the checklist: SIGNET_MASTER_KEY, SIGNET_SESSION_SECRET, SIGNET_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, oidc_client_secret. Deleting an app does not revoke credentials that were issued to it; treat any that were long-lived as compromised-by-default and rotate at the issuer rather than only removing them from Fly.
- signet docs referencing the Fly deployment as a supported target (docs/design/edge-signing-contract.md's issuance-path table lists /callback, /exchange-token and /api/cert/register as "Go authority (Fly)").

NOT actionable from the signet repo alone: the app, its secrets and the process group live in rig; the service binding lives in notme. This bead tracks signet's side (docs, and confirming no signet code path assumes the Fly authority) and the coordination; the destructive steps need whoever holds rig's Fly credentials.
acceptance_criteria: The Fly signet app is removed only after /exchange-token and /api/cert/register are confirmed serving from the edge; the notme VPC_AUTH binding and unmatched-path fallthrough are removed; the rig signet process group, entrypoint and Dockerfile install path are removed; every secret from signet-68751f's inventory is deleted AND rotated at its issuer; and no signet doc still lists Fly as a supported authority deployment.

title: Add wasm FFI layer to signet-sign crate
description:
signet-sign builds as cdylib but exports nothing useful — functions are `pub fn` without `#[no_mangle]` or `wasm-bindgen`. Need a wasm FFI layer so rig's CF Worker can consume the wasm for Ed25519 bridge cert signing.

Options:
1. wasm-bindgen (generates JS glue, npm-publishable)
2. #[no_mangle] extern "C" FFI (raw wasm, caller manages memory)

wasm-bindgen is better for the Worker use case. Functions to expose:
- sign_data(data, signing_key_der, cert_der) → cms_signature
- verify(cms_bytes, cert_der) → bool
- parse_cert(der_bytes) → cert info

Consumer: rig/web/src/auth/signet-edge.ts (currently uses @peculiar/x509)

title: Declare signet-3a6a7c's LLO wasm-artifact wait in a local .vigil.toml
description:
Move this repo's cross-repo wait out of vigil's central config and into a
`.vigil.toml` fragment here, so the repo that OWNS the wait declares it.

## Mechanism (already exists, verified in vigil src/config.rs)

vigil's global config carries `repos = [...]`; each adopted directory
contributes its own `[[watches]]` from a `.vigil.toml` at its root.
`load_effective_config` applies per-repo defaults:

    if watch.repo.local_path.is_none() && watch.repo.remote.is_none() {
        watch.repo.local_path = Some(repo_dir.clone());   // only if BOTH unset
    }
    if watch.bead_repo.is_none() && !watch.bead_ids.is_empty() {
        watch.bead_repo = Some(repo_dir.clone());         // this repo's own store
    }

That fits a cross-repo wait exactly: set `repo.remote` explicitly (which
suppresses the local_path default) and `bead_repo` correctly falls back to
THIS repo. Duplicate watch names across sources are refused loudly, naming
both files. Fragments cannot adopt further repos — no recursion.

## Why it is better than the central file

Today vigil's watches.toml would have to know this repo's bead ids. That is
central inference about someone else's state. A fragment is authored by the
repo that actually holds the bead, versioned in ITS history, and moves with
it. Same discipline as the rest of the release-contract work: declare
locally, do not infer centrally.

## Verify before arming

`vigil run --config <path> --dry-run` reads for real (gh, crates.io, the
bead store) and writes nothing. A watch that would act prints
`WOULD notify <bead-id> (<evidence>)`. Check that line names the right bead
and carries evidence you believe before this fragment goes live.

Caveat: `--dry-run` prints `UNCHECKED` for merge_shaped watches. git_pull's
check IS its pull, so a dry run genuinely cannot exercise that path. Only
tool_poll conditions are verified by it.

## Note on on_resolve

Default is `Close`. For a bead that is BLOCKED-class — real work that could
not start until an external fact was true — use `on_resolve = "comment"`.
Closing such a bead destroys the work item rather than completing it. See
vigil-cbbed3: the default is destructive-on-omission and is being changed.

## This repo's watch

signet-3a6a7c waits on ley-line-open v0.14.0's wasm artifacts. AS OF
2026-08-04 THAT CONDITION IS ALREADY TRUE — v0.14.0 published
2026-07-31T05:23:48Z carrying all four declared assets (leyline_sign.wasm,
leyline_cas_ffi.wasm, leyline_envelope.wasm, SHA256SUMS). Verified by
`vigil run --dry-run`, which printed:

    llo v0.14.0 wasm assets: WOULD notify signet-3a6a7c (release v0.14.0
    published 2026-07-31T05:23:48Z carries all 4 declared assets (...))

So signet-3a6a7c has been unblocked for days and nothing said so. The
fragment below is what makes the NEXT one arrive on its own.

    [[watches]]
    name = "signet: llo wasm artifacts"
    bead_ids = ["signet-3a6a7c"]
    on_resolve = "comment"     # blocked-class: lift the blocker, do not close the work
    [watches.repo]
    remote = "agentic-research/ley-line-open"
    [watches.condition]
    type = "release_assets"
    tag = "v0.14.0"
    assets = ["leyline_sign.wasm", "leyline_cas_ffi.wasm", "leyline_envelope.wasm", "SHA256SUMS"]

Source of truth for the shape: vigil tests/fixtures/watches/ley-line-open-v0.14.0.toml.
Requires vigil's global config to list this directory in `repos`.

comments.text:
MIGRATION CORRECTION — read before writing .vigil.toml. Two things in this
bead's original description were wrong or incomplete.

## 1. The two signet paths are ONE directory, not two

    /Users/jamesgardner/github  ->  /Users/jamesgardner/remotes   (symlink, 2025-02-16)

So `github/art/signet` and `remotes/art/signet` are the same directory —
verified, same inode 16777233:123260920. There is no "old path" to migrate
FROM in any meaningful sense, and nothing is currently broken by it. The
notification vigil wrote to signet-3a6a7c on 2026-08-04 landed exactly once
and is readable through either spelling.

Use `/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/signet` as the canonical form anyway —
one spelling, consistently — but do not treat this as a data migration.

## 2. The real hazard, which this bead originally set up

vigil's global config currently has:

    name = "llo v0.14.0 wasm assets"
    bead_ids = ["signet-3a6a7c"]
    bead_repo = "/Users/jamesgardner/github/art/signet"

and this bead told you to create:

    name = "signet: llo wasm artifacts"     <- DIFFERENT NAME

Different names means vigil's duplicate-name check does NOT fire. Both
watches act on signet-3a6a7c. `notify_marker` is keyed by watch NAME, so
each writes its own `[vigil:...]` marker, neither sees the other's, neither
reaches its terminal state, and signet-3a6a7c collects a fresh pair of
comments on every 15-minute poll, forever.

FIXED IN VIGIL (0d0c7ef): a config where two watches act on the same bead in
the same store is now refused at LOAD, with both watch names and the
canonical store path in the message. Paths are canonicalized first, so the
symlink alias cannot hide the collision. Verified against the real config —
before the fix the half-migration loaded cleanly.

So a half-done migration now fails loudly instead of double-notifying. You
still have to do both halves.

## The migration, corrected

1. Create `/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/signet/.vigil.toml` with BOTH
   watches — this bead's LLO wasm wait and signet-6da4b0's signature-bundle
   watch. One file, one change; they conflict otherwise.
2. In `~/.config/vigil/watches.toml`, DELETE the watch named exactly
   `llo v0.14.0 wasm assets` (bead_ids = ["signet-3a6a7c"]). Leave
   `llo v0.14.0 wasm assets (notme)` alone — different bead, different store.
3. Add `/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/signet` to the top-level `repos`
   list in that same file.
4. `vigil run --config ~/.config/vigil/watches.toml --dry-run` and read it.

Expected after a correct migration: the signet wasm watch reports
`resolved (beads already notified)` — the marker vigil wrote on 2026-08-04
is still there and still terminal, under the OLD watch name. If you rename
the watch, that marker no longer matches and signet-3a6a7c gets a second
comment saying the same thing.

Which is the argument for keeping the name `llo v0.14.0 wasm assets`
verbatim in the fragment rather than the prettier `signet: llo wasm
artifacts` this bead originally suggested. The marker is the terminal state;
renaming the watch resets it.

title: Reconcile PolicyEvaluator (string URIs) vs PolicyChecker (uint64 tokens)
description:
Two parallel policy abstractions exist in pkg/policy/:
- PolicyEvaluator: uses string capability URIs, StaticPolicyEvaluator with allowlists. Used by authority today.
- PolicyChecker: uses uint64 capability token IDs from ADR-010 registry. Trust policy bundles (ADR-011).

These must converge before the authority can use trust policy bundles. Options:
1. PolicyChecker wraps PolicyEvaluator (adapter pattern)
2. Merge into one interface with both string and uint64 capability formats
3. PolicyEvaluator becomes the legacy path, PolicyChecker replaces it

Flagged by sigpol design review (docs/design/sigpol-requirements.md). Blocks authority integration.

- Identity (sigid): OIDC flow, cert minting, session management, handleLogin, handleCallback, handleExchangeToken

Split into:
- authority_identity.go: Authority struct, mintClientCertificate, parsePublicKeyBytes, OIDCServer, session crypto

- authority.go: HTTP mux, rate limiter, server lifecycle, health, landing

title: harden: SIG1 payload is parsed twice pre-authentication in DecodeSIG1
description: Found by adversarial review of PR #152 (signet-62f8e0). DecodeSIG1 (pkg/signet/sig1.go) base64-decodes and fully CBOR-parses the payload via Unmarshal BEFORE any signature verification — and as of the layout-boundary fix that is two CBOR parses (the layout probe into map[any]RawMessage plus the struct decode) on attacker-supplied bytes. VerifySIG1 calls DecodeSIG1 first, then verifies. Today this is not a live production surface (no callers outside pkg/signet), which is why it is not a release blocker, but it becomes one the moment SIG1 is wired into a network path. Options to evaluate: cap the accepted payload size before decoding; verify the COSE signature before the token decode (requires restructuring since the verifier needs the payload bytes, not the parsed token — the bytes are available pre-parse); or document the parse-before-verify ordering as intentional with an explicit input bound. Do not close by asserting 'not exploitable today' — pick a bound or an ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Either the SIG1 decode path enforces an explicit maximum payload size before CBOR parsing, or signature verification precedes token parsing; a test covers the chosen bound/ordering with an oversized or unsigned payload; the decision is recorded in docs/design/001-signet-tokens.md.

title: ci: go-version pins are stale and rely on implicit toolchain auto-download
description: Found by adversarial review of PR #149 (signet-e6a047). .github/workflows/ci.yml pins go-version: '1.23' in the test, test-pkcs11, and benchmark jobs, while go.mod now declares go 1.25.5 (only the security job uses go-version-file: go.mod). Builds still succeed because GOTOOLCHAIN defaults to auto, so the 1.23 binary silently downloads and switches to 1.25.5 from proxy.golang.org at CI time. That is an undeclared network dependency and a version the workflow does not name — inconsistent with this repo's otherwise strict SHA-pinning discipline (see the detailed pin-rationale comments for golangci-lint in the same file). Switch the three jobs to go-version-file: go.mod so the toolchain follows the module declaration explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: No workflow job pins a literal go-version that disagrees with go.mod; the test, test-pkcs11, and benchmark jobs use go-version-file: go.mod; a CI run on the change is green with its run URL recorded on this bead.

title: ci: make a skipped Claude review visible instead of silently green
description: Follow-up from the adversarial review of PR #151 (signet-dd7f9c). The skip fix trades an always-red check for a silently-green one: if CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is later revoked or rotated badly, reviews stop happening and the only signal is a ::notice annotation buried in the Actions log, which nobody reads on a green run. Make the skip state legible — write the reason to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY so it appears on the run page, and consider a periodic check (or vigil watch) that flags when the skip state has persisted across N consecutive PRs. The point is that a disabled reviewer should be observable without anyone remembering to look.
acceptance_criteria: A skipped review writes its reason to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY so it is visible on the run page without opening logs; a run exercising the skip path has its URL recorded on this bead.

title: ADR: signet runtime split — which operations belong at edge (Wasm+TS) vs Go server
description:
Signet serves multiple deployment targets with different runtime constraints. Need an ADR defining the split:

**Edge (CF Worker):** leyline-sign Wasm (276KB, Ed25519+CMS) + TS glue (OIDC JWT via WebCrypto, session via DO). Handles cert exchange, health, landing page — no tunnel roundtrip.

**Server (Go on k8s/Fly):** Full authority — CA ops, key generation, cert chain mgmt, PKCS#11, policy eval, rate limiting. Also CLI (`signet sign`, `signet auth login`, `signet-git`).

Prior art:
- leyline-sign Wasm build verified (rig-959350, closed)
- Landing page already externalized to static file (PR #94)
- rig Worker TS wrapper designed (rig-959350)

Key decision: which authority endpoints can run edge-only vs need Go?

comments.text: Context from session: go-cms is already pure Go (zero C deps). The motivation for Rust/WASM is convergence — eliminate dual Go+TS implementations so signet can run at the CF Worker edge natively. ADR should address: WASM boundary for key material, wazero hosting in Go, CMS crate for git signing, and the BYOC (bring your own CA) distribution model.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
## Discovery: `leyline-sign` crate already exists

`ley-line/rs/crates/sign/` (`leyline-sign` v0.1.0) implements the Rust CMS/PKCS#7 + Ed25519 signing primitives that this ADR proposes. 12 tests pass.

### What's already built:
- **`cms.rs`** (~870 lines) — Full CMS/PKCS#7 SignedData creation + verification (RFC 5652 + RFC 8419). Both signed-attributes and PureEdDSA modes. DER encode/parse from scratch (mirrors go-cms). Weak algorithm rejection (MD5/SHA-1). Constant-time digest comparison.
- **`cert.rs`** — X.509 cert parsing (via `x509-cert` crate), signer identifier extraction, key-match verification.
- **`ffi.rs`** — C FFI (`leyline_sign_data`, `leyline_sign_data_without_attributes`, `leyline_verify`) with buffer-based API. Builds as cdylib + staticlib + rlib.
- **`oid.rs`** — OID constants (id-data, id-signedData, SHA-512, Ed25519, CMS attributes).
- **`error.rs`** — Typed errors (`SignError`, `VerifyError`).
- **`cbindgen.toml`** — C header generation configured.

### Deps (all pure Rust / RustCrypto — Wasm-compatible):
`cms 0.2`, `der 0.7`, `x509-cert 0.2`, `spki 0.7`, `const-oid 0.9`, `ed25519-dalek 2.1`, `sha2 0.10`

### What's missing vs this ADR:
1. **Bridge cert issuance** — signet's `pkg/attest/x509/` (short-lived certs from OIDC claims). Not in leyline-sign.
2. **OIDC JWT validation** — signet's `pkg/oidc/`. Not in leyline-sign.
3. **Capability extensions** — ASN.1 custom extensions for MCP capabilities. Not in leyline-sign.
4. **Wasm build target** — deps are Wasm-compatible but no `wasm32-wasi` target tested yet.
5. **Git signing CLI** — README mentions gpgsm-compatible binary for jj, but no `main.rs` binary yet (only lib).

### Recommendation:
Rename scope of this bead. `leyline-sign` IS the signet-core signing layer. What's needed is:
- Add bridge cert issuance to `leyline-sign` (or a sibling `leyline-attest` crate)
- Add OIDC validation (or a sibling `leyline-oidc` crate) 
- Test wasm32-wasi compilation
- Wire signet Go code to call leyline-sign via FFI (cdylib) or replace go-cms entirely
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
## Rescoping: this is not "rewrite signet in Rust" — it's "split signet along runtime boundaries"

### Discovery (2026-03-23)
- `leyline-sign` (Rust, 276KB Wasm) already covers Ed25519 + CMS/PKCS#7 — the ONLY custom crypto
- `rig-959350` (closed) proved the CF Worker path: Wasm for signing, TS for OIDC/JWT (WebCrypto)
- Go signet authority works fine on Fly/k8s — no reason to replace it

### The real question: what's the split?

Signet today is a single Go binary serving multiple deployment targets that have fundamentally different runtime constraints:

| Runtime | What runs there | Constraints |
|---------|----------------|-------------|
| **CF Worker** (Wasm) | Ed25519 sign/verify, CMS, cert exchange | No filesystem, no long processes, 128MB mem, must be Wasm |
| **CF Worker** (TS) | OIDC JWT validation, session mgmt, DO state | WebCrypto covers JWT, no custom crypto needed |
| **k8s / Fly** (Go) | Full authority server, OIDC provider registry, policy eval, rate limiting, CA | Needs filesystem (keys), long-running process, full stdlib |
| **CLI** (Go) | `signet sign`, `signet auth login`, `signet-git` | Needs OS access, keystore, browser launch |

Go is basically required for k8s/Fly (ecosystem, tooling, existing infra). Wasm is required for CF edge. These aren't competing — they serve different tiers.

### Proposed split (not a rewrite):
1. **signet** (Go, unchanged) — authority server + CLI + k8s operator. The "control plane."
2. **leyline-sign** (Rust→Wasm) — crypto primitives at edge. Already exists, 276KB.
3. **TS glue in rig** — OIDC + session + DO. Calls leyline-sign Wasm for signing. Calls signet authority for full cert chain validation when needed.

### What this bead should become:
NOT "ADR: signet-core in Rust/Wasm" but rather "ADR: signet runtime split — which operations belong at which tier?" The crypto is solved. The architecture question is: which signet authority endpoints can be served entirely at the edge (Wasm+TS) vs which need the full Go server behind a tunnel?

Candidates for edge-only (no Go roundtrip):
- Certificate exchange (Ed25519 sign → Wasm, OIDC verify → WebCrypto)
- Health check
- Landing page (already done — static HTML via rig Dockerfile)

Must stay on Go server:
- Full CA operations (key generation, cert chain management)
- PKCS#11 integration
- Policy evaluation with complex rules
- Rate limiting with persistent state (unless DO handles it)

comments.text:
DISPOSITION for Goal Zero clause 2-4 (signet-bed718) — and a promotion. This bead is NOT deferrable: it is the decision that three other open P1s are silently waiting on, and they currently point in incompatible directions. Just linked signet-3530a4, signet-68751f and signet-c784cf as depending on it.

The fork, stated plainly:

- signet-c784cf — "Port OAuth flows to notme/worker — ELIMINATE the Fly signet process."
- signet-68751f — "Zero-secret FLY DEPLOY — signet delegates signing to auth.notme.bot DO." Hardens the process c784cf retires.
- signet-3530a4 — "Device flow endpoints in the GO AUTHORITY." Its own description notes rig already shipped device flow in TS; this adds the same capability to the process c784cf retires, "so signet can be self-contained".

All three are open P1 with no stated ordering, so a dispatcher could pick any of them and be working against one of the others. Two of them add capability to the Go authority; the third deletes its reason to exist. That is not a prioritisation problem, it is an unmade architectural decision — which is exactly what this bead is for.

Live evidence that the decision is not academic (from the Goal Zero runtime audit, signet-c0a318): the Fly-hosted signet process is DOWN in production right now — /exchange-token and /api/cert/register both return 500 via the Worker's VPC fallthrough, because rig's entrypoint runs /app/signet while the Dockerfile installs to /usr/local/bin/signet. So the "eliminate Fly" direction currently has the facts on its side, and the "harden Fly" direction is investing in something that has never successfully started. Deciding that is worth more than either implementation.

Note on scope, since a user recollection prompted this review: I could not confirm a device-flow tie between notme and cloister. signet-3530a4's own text ties it to rig (which already shipped it) and rosary.bot; searching cloister's beads for device flow returns nothing, and notme's two device-adjacent beads are about invite TTLs and entire.io federation. If there is a real cloister dependency it lives outside the bead stores and should be written down here, because it would change the answer — a downstream consumer waiting on the Go device flow is exactly the cross-repo pull that would override the defer rule.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
DECISION INPUT, from the user: c784cf (eliminate the Fly Go process) is probably the right fork, because leyline-sign exists. Verified the load-bearing part of that argument rather than accepting it, and it holds — with one precise residual.

WHAT I CHECKED. leyline-sign does not use wasm-bindgen, which an earlier reading of docs/design/edge-signing-contract.md ("JS/TS bindings: none exist") treated as a blocker. That reading is misleading. The crate exports a deliberate raw C ABI (rs/ll-open/sign/src/ffi.rs, #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C"), and its export surface is asserted by a test (tests/wasm_export_surface.rs):

  lsign_alloc, lsign_free                      — manual memory management
  leyline_sign_data                            — CMS sign WITH signed attributes (the shape signet's Go path uses)
  leyline_sign_data_without_attributes         — Case 2
  leyline_verify, leyline_verify_cert_chain    — verification + chain

A raw C-ABI module is callable from a Worker with plain WebAssembly.instantiate — alloc, copy bytes in, call, read out, free. That is the normal pattern for Workers, where wasm-bindgen glue is often deliberately avoided. So "no bindings" means "no generated glue", not "not callable". The capability that justified a Go server — CMS signing — genuinely exists at the edge today. The user's argument stands.

THE RESIDUAL, and it is specific rather than hand-wavy. Signing is covered; CERTIFICATE MINTING with signet's semantics is not. rs/ll-open/sign/src/oid.rs contains 7 constants and none of them is under signet's private arc 1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1.* — grep for 99999 returns nothing. Those extensions (OIDSubject, OIDIssuanceTime, OIDSignetCapabilities, OIDAgentName, OIDScope) are what make a signet bridge cert mean anything, and docs/design/edge-signing-contract.md already documents the consequence: when /api/cert/register is served by the edge, the minted cert omits OIDAgentName and OIDScope, so --agent and --scope are silently ignored.

So the honest statement of the fork's answer: leyline-sign removes the SIGNING reason to keep a Go process. It does not yet remove the CERT-MINTING reason. Closing that is a bounded, nameable piece of work — add the signet extension OIDs to the crate (an LLO PR, already listed as prerequisite 2 in edge-signing-contract.md's Wasm Integration Status) — rather than an open-ended objection.

IMPLICATION FOR THE OTHER TWO BEADS, for the ADR to rule on rather than me: if c784cf wins, signet-68751f (harden the Fly deploy) is investing in a process being retired and should close as obsolete rather than defer, and signet-3530a4 (device flow in the Go authority) loses its stated rationale — its own text says it exists "so signet can be self-contained", which is precisely the property c784cf gives up on purpose. Both are already linked here, so whichever way this ADR lands, they resolve with it.

title: master_sk adopts URL-spec resolver (align with cloister ADR-0014 v2)
description:
## What

Adopt the same URL-spec resolver pattern cloister uses for `VAULT_KEK_SOURCE`. Signet's master_sk loader should accept:

- `keychain://<service>` (macOS)
- `secret-tool://<service>` (Linux libsecret)
- `file:///path/to/key.pem` (any platform, including CI)
- `env://VAR` (today: plaintext; future: age-encrypted ciphertext)
- `http(s)://helper/...` (generic helper)

Resolved via a shared trust-anchor-helper sidecar (see linked bead).

## Why

The metavisor / airgapped story (documented in cloister's threat model + ADR-0011/0013/0014) requires that long-term keys never live in plaintext in any process's heap or committed config. Today cloister enforces this for the vault KEK (ADR-0014 v2). Signet holds the master_sk that DSSE-signs artifacts cloister stores in BlobStore — that key is the trust root for the entire substrate.

If cloister enforces no-plaintext but signet doesn't, the trust-anchor chain has a weak link. Aligning means both repos share one model: "all long-term keys in OS keystore / HSM, mediated by a helper, never in heap or config."

## Mirror of

[cloister-127a3c](https://github.com/agentic-research/cloister) — the cross-repo bead in cloister's store that tracks this same work from cloister's perspective.

## Reference materials

- cloister ADR-0014 v2 amendment (docs/adr/0014-pluggable-kek-source.md) — the URL-spec contract this bead adopts
- cloister/vault/src/kek-source.ts — TS reference implementation of the resolver. Go port should mirror the scheme handling.
- cloister-125199 (already shipped) — cloister's enforcement landed

## Suggested files (signet-side)

- `pkg/keysource/` (new) — Go implementation of the URL-spec resolver
- `pkg/keysource/keychain_darwin.go` — macOS Keychain backend via Security framework
- `pkg/keysource/libsecret_linux.go` — Linux libsecret backend
- `pkg/keysource/file.go` — cross-platform file:// backend
- `cmd/signet/authority.go` (or wherever master_sk loads) — refactor to use resolver
- `docs/adr/` — signet-side ADR documenting the alignment
- README — update key-storage section + remove any "plaintext file path" guidance

## Done when

- Signet accepts `SIGNET_MASTER_KEY_SOURCE=keychain://com.notme/master` (or equivalent)
- Same scheme set as cloister: `env://` (encrypted carrier only when v2b lands), `file://`, `keychain://`, `secret-tool://`, `http(s)://`
- Signet's CI uses `file://` with ephemeral path
- Signet throws on empty/missing source (no fallback)
- Signet docs point at the shared trust-anchor-helper for keystore-mediated schemes

## Depends on

- Shared trust-anchor-helper protocol — if `keychain://` is mediated through a helper rather than directly via Security framework

title: Shared trust-anchor-helper protocol (factor out cloister's kek-helper.mjs)
description:
## What

Generalize cloister's `kek-helper.mjs` sidecar into a shared trust-anchor-helper that both cloister's vault DO AND signet's master_sk loader consume. Same binary, same wire protocol.

## Why

- cloister vault needs OS-keystore access (workerd can't shell to `security` / `secret-tool` directly — V8 isolate)
- signet master_sk loader needs the same OS-keystore access — adopting URL-spec resolver
- Without sharing, both repos implement keychain://+secret-tool:// resolution twice and risk divergence

## Wire protocol (proposed)

JSON-over-stdio OR JSON-over-Unix-socket OR HTTP-on-loopback. Cloister's current `kek-helper.mjs` uses HTTP-on-loopback:

```
GET /resolve?url=keychain://com.notme/master
  200 OK
  Content-Type: application/octet-stream
  <raw bytes>

GET /resolve?url=keychain://does-not-exist
  404 Not Found
  Content-Type: application/json
  {"error":"not_found"}
```

For signing operations (where the helper holds the key and signs on behalf of caller — better than `resolve` for long-term keys):

```
POST /sign
  Body: {"url":"keychain://com.notme/master","alg":"ed25519","message_b64":"..."}
  Response: {"ok":true,"signature_b64":"..."}
```

`op: sign` is strongly preferred over `op: resolve` for the master_sk path — the key never leaves the helper, only signatures cross the wire.

## Mirror of

[cloister-12b062](https://github.com/agentic-research/cloister) — the cross-repo bead in cloister's store.

## Implementation options

1. **Standalone repo** (`trust-anchor-helper` / `tah`) — both cloister and signet depend on it via release artifact
2. **In signet's tree** (`cmd/trust-anchor-helper/`) — signet owns the binary, cloister consumes
3. **In each repo with shared SPEC.md** — duplication but no cross-repo coupling

Lean toward option 2 (signet owns it) because:
- signet's domain IS trust roots / signing
- Go is the right language (talks to OS Security framework / libsecret natively)
- cloister's kek-helper.mjs becomes a thin Node port-of-protocol for cases where the Go binary isn't appropriate

## Suggested files

- `cmd/trust-anchor-helper/main.go` (new)
- `pkg/keystore/keychain_darwin.go`
- `pkg/keystore/libsecret_linux.go`
- `pkg/keystore/file.go`
- `docs/trust-anchor-helper-spec.md` (canonical protocol spec)
- `Taskfile.yml` / Makefile — build target

## Done when

- One binary, two consumers (cloister vault DO, signet master_sk loader)
- Protocol spec'd in `docs/trust-anchor-helper-spec.md`
- Both `op: resolve` (returns bytes) AND `op: sign` (key stays in helper) implemented
- macOS Keychain + Linux libsecret + file:// all working
- cloister's `scripts/kek-helper.mjs` deprecated with a pointer at this binary
- cloister's tests pass against the new helper (vitest stub remains identical because the wire is the same)

## Coordinated with

- signet master_sk URL-spec adoption (sibling bead in signet)
- cloister-127a3c / cloister-12b062 (cloister-side coordination)
- cloister-125199 (already shipped — cloister's vault now requires the resolver)

title: Define the canonical protocol-kid derivation + emit pinned cross-language test vectors (trust-root authority)
description:
Signet owns the canonical `kid` that binds a signed Σ head / bridge cert / JWK to a resolvable Ed25519 public key. Today three repos derive `kid` three incompatible ways, so no verifier can resolve an LLO head's `signerKid` against notme's JWKS:

- LLO (Rust):   BLAKE3(raw 32-byte Ed25519 pubkey)[..8]      — 64 bits
- notme (TS):   RFC-7638-ish truncated SHA-256 over SPKI DER — 64 bits
- signet (Go):  generateSubjectKeyID = SHA-1 over raw/SPKI   — 160 bits (X.509 SubjectKeyId)

DECISION (locked with @jamestexas 2026-07-21):
- Canonical derivation = `BLAKE3(raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key)`, truncated to 128 bits (16 bytes). BLAKE3 keeps LLO scoped to a single hash — the one intentional Σ seam. Raw key (not SPKI DER) removes encoding ambiguity across languages. 128 bits (not LLO's current 64) so a trust-root-adversary can't lean on ~2^32 birthday cost even though kid is selection-not-authorization.
- Hash choice is safe because JWK `kid` is opaque per RFC 7517 §4.5 — notme's own consumers opaque-match (`keys.find(k => k.kid === header.kid)`, worker.js:37085), never recompute RFC-7638. Cloudflare Access sits UPSTREAM of notme (notme verifies CF JWTs), so nobody external recomputes notme's kid. Verified 2026-07-21.
- signet's existing SHA-1 `generateSubjectKeyID` STAYS as the X.509 SubjectKeyId cert field (RFC 5280 §4.2.1.2) — a separate concern, untouched.

Deliverables:
1. ADR in signet/docs/ defining the canonical kid (hash, input encoding, width, versioning — a change is v2, not an edit).
2. `Kid(ed25519.PublicKey) []byte` (or similar) in signet/pkg, plus its inverse discipline (kid is not reversible; document that it selects, never authorizes).
3. A pinned vector fixture (JSON or capnp) shipping known (pubkey -> kid) pairs, committed to signet and consumed by LLO/notme/cloister CI. leyline-net/v1 pinned-bytes discipline: changing a vector is a breaking protocol event.

Close condition: `cd ~/remotes/art/signet && go test ./pkg/... -run Kid` green AND the vector fixture file exists and is referenced by the ADR.

comments.text:
Thread anchor — signed-roots-spine/canonical-kid (decade: signed-roots-spine).

This bead is the AUTHORITY: signet defines the one canonical protocol-kid = BLAKE3(raw 32-byte Ed25519 pubkey) truncated 128-bit. The other three conform and gate on the pinned vectors this bead ships (all depend_on signet-248d17):
- ley-line-open-24bd97 (S3) — resolve signerKid + widen 64→128-bit
- notme-254f03 — replace keyIdFromSpki with canonical kid, epoch-rotate JWKS
- cloister-2508ec — conform root-verify + retire duplicate trust-root crate; blocks cloister-9b03c4 (S6)

Spine context: S1 (sign) + S2 (verify-on-load) shipped in ley-line-open PR #247 (bead ley-line-open-f8eda9). S6 (cloister authoritative mount) is cloister-9b03c4. This thread is S3, the trust-root layer that makes S2/S6 able to RESOLVE a kid, not just verify a pre-configured key.

NOTE: the structured `acceptance_criteria` field read back empty on create — the known rosary-4887d0 silent-drop bug. Every bead in this thread carries its close condition as a `Close condition:` line in the description prose; use that as the gate.

Decision provenance: hash=BLAKE3 (LLO stays one-hash, the single intentional Σ seam), width=128-bit (birthday margin over LLO's current 64), input=raw key (no SPKI DER ambiguity). Safe because JWK kid is opaque per RFC 7517 §4.5 — notme consumers opaque-match, never recompute; Cloudflare Access is upstream of notme. Verified 2026-07-21.

description: From the type-driven integration review of signet-62f8e0. The boundary's guarantees are currently pinned by hand-picked example vectors; two of them are universally-quantified properties that deserve fuzz targets (the repo already has fuzz precedent in pkg/revocation/fuzz_test.go). P1 — the boundary's actual claim: for all byte sequences b, if Unmarshal(b) succeeds then b's top-level map contains no key that is not a non-negative integer AND contains at least one of keys 7/9/13. Implement as FuzzUnmarshal seeded with the two golden vectors; on success, re-probe b with an independent lenient decoder and assert the key-set predicate. title: Capnp-ify MasterKeyDescriptor: move into notme/schema/identity.capnp via schema-bridge
description:
## Problem
L10 (`signet-965dc7` / commit `8a79f9a`) introduced a NEW type `MasterKeyDescriptor { IssuerDID, TrustDomain string }` in `signet/pkg/signet/signet.go`. The subagent created it because no existing master-key descriptor struct existed in signet.

That capnp file is the cross-language source of truth and already generates Go (`$Go.package("identity"); $Go.import("github.com/agentic-research/notme/gen/go/identity");`), TypeScript, and Zod via schema-bridge.

L10's MasterKeyDescriptor is duplicate work that lives in a Go-only file. It should be generated from notme/schema/identity.capnp instead.

title: kid canonicalization: notme hashes SPKI as-received, diverges from signet on non-canonical DER (R2)
description: [red-team:trust-root] Trust-root adversarial review of ADR signet-248d17 (docs/design/012). VERIFIED empirically (independent recompute this session): notme keyIdFromSpki (worker/src/key-id.ts:31) hashes the SPKI bytes AS-RECEIVED (atob then SHA-256, no re-canonicalization). signet MachineFingerprint (pkg/sigid/identity.go:72) re-marshals via x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey. So for any non-canonical DER they DISAGREE on the kid. Demonstrated: same Ed25519 key, absent-params DER (302a300506032b6570...) vs NULL-params DER (302c300706032b65700500...) -> kid128 9408457aefd071cec127c1f985399308 vs 694c79f433516b1402170355d98eb229. Blocks notme-254f03 conformance.

title: kid 64->128 migration keeps 2^64 second-preimage floor until flag-day; prevKeyId carries raw 64-bit (R3)
description: [red-team:trust-root] Trust-root review of signet-248d17. Prefix-compatibility (kid64 = kid128[:16 hex]) is a migration nicety but keeps the second-preimage floor at 2^64 for as long as ANY 64-bit comparator lives — and prefix-compat is precisely what keeps them alive. rotate() writes the raw 64-bit oldKeyId into prevKeyId (worker/src/signing-authority.ts:487), compared by === at worker/src/revocation.ts:364. During the grace window an attacker could present a key whose 64-bit prefix matches a victim's prevKeyId (2^64 reachable) even though the 128-bit ids differ. FIX: hard flag-day rejecting 64-bit derivation; full-length compares only; re-derive prevKeyId at 128-bit on boundary rotation. Depends on notme-254f03. Not a merge blocker for the ADR (safe to ratify per the review), but must land before the migration window opens.
acceptance_criteria: no 64-bit kid comparator remains: a flag-day rejects 64-bit-width derivation, all kid compares are full-length, and prevKeyId is re-derived at 128-bit on the rotation boundary (not the raw 64-bit value)

title: MCP transport security via signet HTTP middleware
description:
## Problem

MCP (Model Context Protocol) has no authentication story. Tool calls over HTTP
are unsigned JSON-RPC — any client can invoke any tool with no proof of identity.

## Proposal

Use signet's existing HTTP middleware (`pkg/http/middleware`) to sign/verify
MCP tool calls over the streamable HTTP transport:

1. **Sign tool calls** — agent signs each `tools/call` request with an ephemeral
   cert. MCP server verifies proof-of-possession.
2. **Sign tool results** — server signs responses so agents can verify provenance.
3. **Wrap mache serve** — signet middleware around `mache serve --http` endpoint.

stdio transport doesn't need this (same trust boundary — subprocess).

## Prior Art

- signet already has `middleware.SignetMiddleware` with clock skew, master key verification
- ley-line ADR-004 planned signet for manifest signing — same pattern applies to MCP
- MCP spec has no auth section; this would be a novel contribution

## Files

- pkg/http/middleware/ (existing middleware)
- New: pkg/mcp/ or integration in mache's serve.go

title: ci: setup-task hit the runner IP's unauthenticated GitHub API limit, failing a data-only PR
description:
Observed on PR #165, whose only change was .beads/beads.jsonl — a data file no Go test reads. The PKCS#11 job failed anyway, at the Install Task step, with: "API rate limit exceeded for 20.168.103.56".

Root cause, and it is worth stating precisely because the symptom points away from it: arduino/setup-task resolves the Task release through the GitHub API, and made that call UNAUTHENTICATED. Unauthenticated GitHub API calls are limited to 60/hr PER SOURCE IP, and hosted runners share IPs across many customers — so the step fails whenever the runner's neighbours have exhausted that shared budget. Confirmed the limit was NOT ours: `gh api rate_limit` from this machine reported 4993/5000 remaining at the same moment. The failing quota belonged to the runner's IP, not to this repository or its token.

Why it matters beyond one flake: the failure is non-deterministic, attributed to whichever job happens to run when a neighbour is noisy, and lands on PRs that cannot possibly have caused it. That is the worst shape of CI failure — it trains reviewers to re-run red checks reflexively, which is exactly the habit that lets a real failure through. It also lands on the release train, where a spurious red on a tag build would be read as a signing problem.

Fix: pass repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} to every setup-task invocation, which authenticates the release lookup and raises the ceiling to 5000/hr against our own quota. Four call sites: ci.yml (x2 — test and test-pkcs11), oidc-signing.yml, signet-resign.yml. GITHUB_TOKEN is already available under each job's existing contents: read permission; no permission change required.

title: sigstore-kms-signet has no CI-usable key path — the only options in Actions are worse than keyless
description:
## Problem

`cmd/sigstore-kms-signet` is a real Sigstore KMS plugin (implements `kms.SignerVerifier` via `signature/kms/cliplugin/handler`), so `cosign sign --key signet://default` produces a standard cosign signature — the object supply-chain scanners actually count. That makes it the natural way for repos in this org to sign artifacts under a signet-rooted identity instead of an ephemeral Fulcio one.

It is not reachable from GitHub Actions without making key handling worse. The plugin loads from OS keyring or `~/.signet/master.key` (`cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/main.go` header). Neither exists on a runner, so a consumer has exactly two options:

1. **Put `SIGNET_MASTER_KEY` in GitHub secrets.** This is the posture `gha-identity.yml`'s own header says that workflow exists to eliminate — verbatim: *"notme.bot → bridge cert pair (eliminates SIGNET_MASTER_KEY in GH)"*. Adopting the plugin this way would undo the thing the identity workflow was built for.

2. **Use the notme.bot bridge Ed25519 signing cert.** No secret, but the same header states private keys *"never leave the action process memory by design"* and consumers *"must instead invoke the action in the same job/step where the keys are used."* That constraint does not compose with a matrix build that produces artifacts in one job and signs in another — which is the shape of most release workflows, including this repo's.

## Evidence that the gap is real rather than theoretical

`signet`'s own `release.yml:134` signs with **keyless** cosign (`cosign sign-blob --yes`, Fulcio OIDC via `sigstore/cosign-installer`), not with `signet://`. The repo does not dogfood its own plugin in CI. That is the strongest available signal that no CI-shaped path currently exists.

## Why this is being filed now

ley-line-open is closing `ley-line-open-9abefd` (LLO publishes unsigned OCI images — provenance attestation is attached via `attest-build-provenance` with `push-to-registry: true`, but there is no cosign-format image signature, which is what scanners count as "signed"). signet was the preferred signer. On investigation LLO is going with keyless cosign for now, because it needs no secret and matches what signet chose for itself. `--key signet://default` is a drop-in swap for the keyless flags later, so nothing is foreclosed — but the swap is not currently possible.

This is a report from a consumer, not a claim on signet's roadmap. The framing may be wrong; the observation is that there is no documented middle path between "keyless" and "master key as a repo secret."

## Possible shapes (signet's call, not the reporter's)

- A companion reusable workflow to `gha-identity.yml` that exposes signing itself, so the same-step key constraint is satisfied *inside* signet's workflow and consumers pass in a digest and get a signature back.
- A KMS plugin mode that accepts a bridge cert / short-lived key from the notme.bot exchange rather than requiring keyring or master key on disk.
- An explicit docs statement that CI signing is keyless-only by design and `signet://` is a workstation-scope trust root — which would also be a complete resolution, and would have answered this in ten seconds.

## References

- `cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/main.go` — key loading, `signet://<key-id>` URI scheme
- `.github/workflows/gha-identity.yml` — `workflow_call`, bridge cert pair, the two constraints quoted above
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:69,84-89,134` — keyless signing in practice
- `docs/sigstore-integration.md` — documents `sign-blob --key signet://default` (workstation flow)
- Consumer: `ley-line-open-9abefd`

title: Least-privilege GitHub token scoping for agent onboarding
description:
Current GH token has way too many permissions: delete repos, full control of private repos, update workflows, create gists, full SSH key control. An agent getting onboarded via signet auth register should need MUCH less.

Minimum viable scopes for an agent:
- repo (read) — to clone and read code
- contents (write) — to push commits to branches
- pull_requests (write) — to create PRs
- NO: delete repos, admin, SSH keys, gists, workflows, org management

This is the onboarding flow:
1. Human authenticates via OAuth (needs broader scopes)
2. Human requests bridge cert for agent (POST /api/cert/bootstrap)
3. Agent uses bridge cert for mTLS — no GH token needed for MCP access
4. Agent needs a SEPARATE, scoped GH token ONLY for git push/PR creation

Design questions:
- Should signet mint a GitHub App installation token (scoped per-repo) instead of using the human's PAT?
- Should the bridge cert itself carry repo scope claims that the orchestrator enforces?
- How does this relate to the CF for SaaS design (rig-0c27c2)?

Related: PR agentic-research/signet#108 (agent-scoped certs), notme.bot/architecture (auth flow docs)

title: Tag immutability is now enforced by GitHub, not just by plan convention
description:
docs/release/goal-zero-promotion.md §5 states "Tags are immutable: never deleted, never moved, never re-signed in place." Until now that was a convention a tired human could violate at 2am. It is now a repository rule.

APPLIED to agentic-research/signet: ruleset id 20526150, name "immutable-tags", target tag, enforcement active, scope ~ALL (every tag, not just v*), rules: deletion + non_fast_forward + update.

VERIFIED BY ATTEMPTING THE VIOLATIONS, not by trusting the API response:
- force-move a tag → "GH013: Repository rule violations found ... Cannot update this protected ref"
- delete a tag → "[remote rejected] ... push declined due to repository rule violations"

Both were rejected against a throwaway probe tag, which was then removed via the escape hatch below and does not persist.

ESCAPE HATCH, documented because a rule with no known recovery path gets disabled in a panic and never re-enabled: PUT the ruleset with enforcement=disabled, perform the removal, PUT enforcement=active, then confirm rules are intact. Exercised end to end while cleaning up the probe tag. Requires admin on the repo.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the release plan's burn rule (a failed rc is burned, never deleted, never reused) only means something if the tag genuinely cannot be reused. Three rc tags now stand as an immutable record of three distinct attempts. Had rc.1 been quietly deleted and re-cut after the first failure, the evidence that production was running eight-day-old code would have been erased along with it.

SAFETY CAVEAT for anyone applying this elsewhere: immutable tags BREAK the standard GitHub Actions convention of re-pointing a floating major tag (v1, v2) at each release. Any repo that ships an action.yml or a reusable workflow, or that has bare vN tags alongside vN.M.P tags, will have its release process broken by this rule. signet is safe because it pins consumers by SHA and its own composite action is referenced by path, not tag. An org-wide audit of which repos are safe is running separately.

comments.text:
ORG-WIDE AUDIT RECORDED (read-only; no settings changed outside signet). 13 public, non-fork, non-archived repos in agentic-research.

WITHOUT tag immutability — all twelve non-signet repos. Signet's ruleset is the only tag protection anywhere in the org; every repo returns 404 on the legacy /tags/protection endpoint.

Those that publish tags today, so the gap is real rather than theoretical: mache (39 tags), ley-line-open (53+, including Go module path tags), rosary (13), notme (8), go-cms (2), go-platform-signers (1), cloister (1), x-ray (1). Four have no tags at all and can be enabled pre-emptively with zero risk: assay, 0day-api, canonical-hours, .github.

WHERE IT WOULD BE UNSAFE: NOWHERE — and this is the result worth recording, because it is the opposite of what I cautioned. I flagged that immutable tags break the Actions floating-major-tag convention (re-pointing v1/v2 per release). The org has ZERO floating major tags: every tag in all 13 repos was checked against ^v[0-9]+$ with no matches. Everything is full semver (v0.21.1) or a Go module path tag (clients/go/leyline-schema/v0.18.0) — and Go module tags must never move anyway, so immutability matches how they are already used.

Both action-shaped repos are safe on direct evidence, not inference:
- notme is the org's only genuine Action (action/action.yml, consumed as agentic-research/notme/action@<ref>). Its own action/README.md REJECTS the floating-tag convention — it lists `@v1` as "bad — mutable", cites the March 2026 Trivy/Aqua tag-hijack, and mandates full commit-SHA pinning. Immutability reinforces its documented contract rather than breaking it. (Note the pleasing symmetry: that is the same incident APAS §1.1 uses as its motivating precedent.)
- signet and notme each publish a reusable workflow (gha-identity.yml, on: workflow_call). The only consumer found, private repo rig, pins by SHA. No tag ref to break — and signet's ruleset is already active, so this is confirmed in practice rather than predicted.

TWO CAVEATS TO CARRY:
1. A ~ALL scope also freezes non-semver marker tags. Three exist: signet:development-history, x-ray:pre-public-v1, and notme's dpop-v0.4.0/v0.2.0/v0.1.0 component tags. None looks like a movable pointer, but if any is used as one, scope that repo's ruleset to v* instead of ~ALL.
2. Org-level rulesets could not be checked — gh api orgs/agentic-research/rulesets needs the admin:org scope the token lacks. The per-repo endpoint surfaces inherited org rulesets in most cases and showed nothing tag-targeted outside signet, so this is low risk, but it is unverified rather than verified. Run `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:org` to close it.

Also checked: jamestexas's three public non-fork repos (agents, smelt-fork, parked) have no tags, no rulesets, no action files — nothing to protect.

A tested standalone script to apply this elsewhere was delivered separately (idempotent, reads the ruleset back rather than trusting the POST, and refuses on action-shaped/floating-tag repos unless --force).

acceptance_criteria: The signet repo has an active tag ruleset blocking deletion and movement, verified by an attempted violation being rejected; and docs/release/goal-zero-promotion.md §5 states that tag immutability is enforced by repository rule with the admin recovery path recorded.

title: Adopt mache find-smells composite action in CI (structural smell ratchet)
description:
First per-repo adoption of the mache W6.1 find-smells composite action (mache tracking epic: mache-571b62; capability shipped in mache PR #480 / bead mache-4dbad9). Enforces structural smells on signet the same way mache self-ratchets: existing debt grandfathered via a committed baseline, only NEW findings fail CI.

       - uses: agentic-research/mache/.github/actions/find-smells@<sha>

description: Signet inserted new Token fields into the integer-key CBOR map and shifted existing semantics: the historical v0.0.1 map used keys 1 issuer, 2 confirmation, 3 expiry, 4 nonce, 5 ephemeral key, 6 not-before, while current Token uses keys 1 issuer, 4 expiry, 5 not-before, 9 confirmation, 17 nonce, 18 ephemeral key. comments.text:
PR #152 (branch fix/signet-62f8e0-sig1-compat) implements the boundary; adversarial review found and I fixed two real defects in the first cut — both worth recording because they are the kind of thing that would have shipped looking correct:

BLOCKER (commit a4bb67f): the detector probed with map[int64]cbor.RawMessage, which FAILS OUTRIGHT on a payload carrying any non-integer key — so appending {"x": 0} to a legacy payload skipped the boundary entirely and fell back to whatever incidental type mismatch the struct decode produced (exactly the failure mode this bead exists to remove). Reproduced independently before fixing. Now the probe decodes into map[any]RawMessage and rejects any non-integer key outright (the schema is integer-keyed exclusively), then requires one of 7/9/13; out-of-int64-range keys count as non-integer. Evasion tests: text, negative-int, bool, float, byte-string (hand-assembled — no Go map-key representation), out-of-range, and a current-format token carrying an extra text key.

MAJOR (commit 8fb673c): duplicate CBOR map keys were accepted with DIVERGENT tie-breaking — generic map decode keeps the last occurrence, struct decode keeps the first. A payload duplicating key 9 could let the probe inspect one confirmation value while the token binds another. Both decodes now share tokenDecMode (DupMapKeyEnforcedAPF); duplicates are a decode error, pinned by test.

Verified clean by review: golden vectors honest (manually decoded, byte-for-byte), no legitimate producer in signet or notme emits tokens lacking 7/9/13.

Residual, filed separately rather than silently accepted: DecodeSIG1 calls Unmarshal before signature verification, so both CBOR parses run pre-auth. Not yet a live surface (no callers outside pkg/signet) but it is an unauthenticated parse path — see the follow-up bead.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Integration review (dataflow + type-driven agents, run on the combined branch) found TWO more gaps in this fix, both now closed on integration/goal-zero-release-fixes (commit 7f43cad, PR #153):

3. The probe still failed OPEN for maps. Three key encodings decode to unhashable Go values — CBOR array (80), map (a0), negative bignum (c349...) — so the probe itself errors, and the earlier revision treated any probe error as "not a map" and passed the payload through to the struct decode. That is the incidental-type-mismatch path this bead exists to eliminate, reachable by construction. Fixed: map-ness is decided from the CBOR head byte (major type 5, data[0]&0xE0 == 0xA0), so only genuine non-maps fall through. Duplicate-key probe failures are now reported as themselves rather than misattributed to the legacy layout — a duplicate key is malformedness, not a layout violation, and the error message should not lie about which.

4. tokenDecMode's strictness stopped at the package edge. pkg/sigid decoded the SAME token wire bytes with plain cbor.Unmarshal (library default: duplicate keys accepted, last-wins) at token_ext.go:44/:81 and providers/cell/provider.go:66 — the latter documented as "the primary method for production use". The desync this bead removed inside pkg/signet had simply relocated to between two packages. Fixed: TokenDecMode() exported with a doc comment stating the requirement, and all three sigid token-bytes sites use it; cross-package regression test at pkg/sigid/token_ext_strictdecode_test.go.

Evasion table extended to the decoder's full key domain (adds nil, cbor.SimpleValue, time.Time, plus the three hand-assembled unhashable encodings). Full suite + vet clean; CI green on PR #153.

Two properties the type reviewer identified as deserving fuzz coverage rather than example vectors are filed as signet-27bb57 — not folded in here because they are new test infrastructure, not a fix to this boundary.

title: Cap'n Proto schemas for cross-language type parity (CABundle, GHAClaims, APAS predicates)
description:
CRITICAL: TypeScript signs CABundles with JSON + alphabetical key sort. Go signs with CBOR canonical encoding. These produce different byte sequences — cross-language verification will fail silently.

Cap'n Proto solves this: deterministic binary format, identical bytes across TS/Go/Rust from same .capnp schema. ley-line already uses capnp (rs/ll/net/schema/manifest.capnp).

Types that need .capnp definitions:
1. CABundle (revocation) — epoch, seqno, keys, keyId, signature
2. TokenClaims (revocation check) — keyId, epoch
3. GitHubActionsClaims (OIDC) — 12+ fields, TS uses Zod, Go uses struct
4. BridgeCertResult — certificate PEM, expires_at, subject
5. APAS predicates — DispatchDefinition, RunDetails, Handoff (from rosary)
6. RevocationReason — enum (epoch_mismatch, unknown_key, rollback_attack, bundle_invalid, bundle_stale)

Ecosystem: capnp-ts for TS (needs CF Workers compat testing), go-capnproto2 for Go (mature), capnpc-rust for Rust (mature). ley-line already has working capnp in Rust.

comments.text: Staleness check (2026-04-12): The CBOR canonical encoding cross-language issue is now explicitly documented as a forward-compat constraint in pkg/revocation/checker.go (PR #119). Comment warns that fxamacker/cbor upgrades can silently break bundle signatures. This doesn't solve the problem (Cap'n Proto still the right fix) but the risk is now documented. Also: pkg/revocation/checker.go removed fragile string error matching — storage implementations MUST use sentinel errors now.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
PR #128 ships the **discoverability** half of this bead.

**Finding from the audit:** The capnp schemas for `CABundle`, `GHAClaims`, `DispatchPredicate`, `HandoffPredicate`, `BridgeCertPair`, etc. **already exist** as the single source of truth at `notme/schema/identity.capnp` (220 lines, with Go/TS/Rust codegen wired). signet's README already credits it in the "Recent (v0.2.0)" section, and the SPIFFE/Sigstore vocab maps reference it.

So the type-parity story is solved. The remaining problems are:

1. **Discoverability** (this PR closes it) — `docs/design/cross-language-schema.md` consolidates the scattered pointers, lists every canonical type by category (revocation/certs/auth/APAS/oracle), lists signet-only types NOT in capnp (`MasterKeyDescriptor` → signet-2f6b68; `Token` CBOR fields → no bead; sigid types → signet-a8e3a7), and spells out the "schema PR to notme first" contract.

2. **Wire-format divergence** (NOT in this PR) — the bead body opens with the CBOR-vs-JSON byte-divergence claim. That is a functional bug, not a schema-sync issue. The capnp schema does not resolve it (schema parity ≠ wire-format parity). The doc explicitly names this as an "Open contract gap (deferred)" — needs its own bead to pick one canonical encoding and deprecate the other.

**Recommend:** Keep this bead open after PR #128 merges. Change its scope to ONLY the wire-format-divergence contract gap (the actual functional bug). Or close this one and spawn a fresh P0 bead with the narrower title "Pick canonical-bytes encoding for CABundle: CBOR-only or JSON-only" — that one is going to need a real decision (which other apex consumer of CABundle exists? which encoding wins on the read path?) and a deprecation window.

User flagged this work as "nothing functional ideally" for now, so the contract-gap part is genuinely deferred work, not a same-PR follow-up.

title: Zero-secret Fly deploy — signet delegates signing to auth.notme.bot DO
description:
Current signet on Fly requires 3 secrets: SIGNET_SESSION_SECRET (env), oidc_client_secret (config), master_key_path (file).

This bead's goal was to get the Fly-hosted signet process from 3 secrets down to zero by delegating certificate signing to auth.notme.bot's SigningAuthority DO over the VPC tunnel. title: Watch the next signet release for its signature bundles — signing is merged but has never run
description:
The secretless signing path is MERGED AND UNPROVEN. Nothing has exercised it,
and the first thing that does will be a real release. This bead is the watch
that reports whether it worked, on the first run, without anyone remembering
to look.

## State, measured 2026-08-04

    latest release   v0.2.1, 2026-03-22
    its assets       checksums-sha256.txt, signet-darwin-arm64,
                     signet-linux-amd64, signet-linux-arm64
                     -> no .sigstore.json, no .pem, nothing attesting
    unreleased       57 commits since v0.2.1
    signing landed   TODAY: 24e9d1e (signet-9b0ecd), 8af4e08 (signet-579491)

So `release.yml` now signs and verifies, and the newest published release
predates that by four months. The next tag is the first execution of this
code in anger.

## Exact assets to watch for — read from source, not guessed

`cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact.go:29-36` (`artifactOutputPaths`)
emits four files per artifact:

    <artifact>.sigstore.json     bundle
    <artifact>.signet.crt.pem    leaf cert
    <artifact>.signet.ca.pem     CA bundle
    <artifact>.signet.pub        ephemeral public key

`release.yml` signs four inputs: signet-darwin-arm64, signet-linux-amd64,
signet-linux-arm64, checksums-sha256.txt. So a complete release carries
4 binaries/checksums + 16 signing artifacts + the originals.

Do NOT hand-type these into the watch from this bead. Re-read
`artifactOutputPaths` when you write it — if the suffixes have changed, the
watch must change with them, and a stale asset name produces a watch that
waits forever while reporting a calm "not yet". That failure mode is the
whole reason this bead spells out where the names live rather than just
listing them.

## The watch

Add to `.vigil.toml` at this repo root (see signet-0e0a6b, which introduces
that file for the LLO wasm wait — do both in one change):

    [[watches]]
    name = "signet: next release is signed"
    bead_ids = []              # observation only; writes to no bead store
    [watches.repo]
    remote = "agentic-research/signet"
    [watches.condition]
    type = "release_assets"
    tag = "<the next tag>"
    assets = [
      "signet-linux-amd64.sigstore.json",
      "signet-darwin-arm64.sigstore.json",
      "signet-linux-arm64.sigstore.json",
      "checksums-sha256.txt.sigstore.json",
    ]

`release_assets` is deliberate and not interchangeable with `release_tag`: a
tag can exist and the release be published while the signing step failed or
its assets never uploaded. That distinction is the condition entire reason
for existing. `bead_ids = []` means no `on_resolve` is needed and nothing is
written anywhere — it observes and prints.

Verify before arming: `vigil run --config <path> --dry-run`. It reads for
real and writes nothing.

## Why this is worth a P1 rather than being left to notice later

signet is the identity component — signet-9b0ecd own words: its binaries are
what other systems here trust to establish identity. Two failure modes are
both silent from outside:

1. Signing breaks and the release ships unsigned. `release.yml` verifies
   what it signed BEFORE creating the release, which should turn this into a
   failed run rather than a bad release — but that guard has never fired in
   production either, so it is a design claim, not an observed one.
2. Signing works and nobody confirms it, so the first person to actually
   check is whoever is investigating an incident.

## Related, and the reason this pattern matters beyond signet

This repo just solved, correctly, a problem vigil spent 2026-08-04 working
around. `fence_report` (vigil-2aadea) reads egress-enforcement evidence out
of a GitHub JOB LOG, which GitHub expires — see openai/fence#154. Signet
publishes its evidence as RELEASE ASSETS: durable, publicly fetchable, and
checkable by a condition vigil already had. Producer-published evidence beats
observer-scraped evidence, and this is the working example.

Contrast worth keeping in view: ley-line-open-a03156 — LLO release workflow
is green for v0.15.0 and v0.15.1 while publishing no crates at all (crates.io
still at 0.14.0, `cargo publish` appears nowhere in that repo). Green release,
missing surface, nothing reporting it. Same class of hole this watch closes
for signet.

comments.text:
PR #146 reviewed. The fragment is correct — and one line in it is a guess
worth knowing about before the fragment gets REGISTERED (it is inert until
then, so this is not a merge blocker).

## Correct, confirmed against source

- `name = "llo v0.14.0 wasm assets"` kept verbatim, with a comment saying
  why. That is what stops signet-3a6a7c getting a second comment: the
  notify marker is keyed by watch name and the existing marker is the
  terminal state.
- `bead_repo` omitted — right. load_effective_config defaults it to the
  adopted dir when bead_ids is non-empty, i.e. signet's own store.
- `[watches.repo] remote = ...` set explicitly, which suppresses the
  local_path default. Correct for a cross-repo wait.
- Second watch has `bead_ids = []`, so no on_resolve is needed. Correct.
- `.sigstore.json` suffixes match cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact.go
  `artifactOutputPaths`, not the workflow's prose. Correct.

## The guess: tag = "v0.2.2"

signet is at v0.2.1 with 57 unreleased commits, and 8af4e08 is
`feat(sigstore): add secretless CI artifact signing`. Under semver a feat
bumps the MINOR — v0.3.0 is at least as likely as v0.2.2, and pre-1.0
practice in this ecosystem has been minor-bumps-for-features (LLO went
0.13 -> 0.14 -> 0.15 on feature releases).

If signet cuts v0.3.0, this watch reports `not yet (release v0.2.2 not
found (not cut yet?))` forever. It will look healthy. Nothing distinguishes
"waiting for a release that has not happened" from "waiting for a release
that will never happen because the version was guessed wrong" — the watch
becomes unfalsifiable, which is the failure mode this repo's own §6.0 rule
exists to prevent, pointed at itself.

## Mitigations, in order of preference

1. WAIT to register this fragment until signet's next tag is actually cut,
   then set the real version. Costs nothing; the fragment is inert.
2. Set the tag at release time as part of cutting it — the release PR
   updates .vigil.toml in the same change that bumps the version.
3. Blocked on vigil: there is no "latest release" condition. Every vigil
   condition names an exact tag, so every fragment is one release from
   silently stale. `latest_release_assets` would make "the NEXT release,
   whatever it is called, carries these bundles" expressible — which is what
   this watch actually means. `gh release view` with no tag argument already
   returns the latest, and it can reuse interpret_release_assets with the
   evidence naming the tag observed. Tracked against vigil-11d5c0, which
   raised the same version-churn problem for fragments generally.

Recommend (1) now and (3) as the durable fix.

## Unrelated, verified while here: vigil-267f8c has no portability problem

The concern that `.github/actions/sign-artifact` builds from signet's own
source does not bite a consuming repo. The action installs Go itself
(`go-version-file: ${{ github.action_path }}/../../../go.mod`), and GitHub
checks out the WHOLE repo for a remote composite action, so
`cd $SIGNET_ACTION_PATH/../../..` lands on signet's root with cmd/ present.
A Rust repo can consume it with no Go setup of its own.

An unknown condition type is a config PARSE failure, not a per-watch error.
vigil exits having processed NOTHING — all 20 watches down, including the
three already-notified ones and every merge_shaped pull. Had the swap
landed, the next scheduled tick would have been a total outage rather than
one wrong line.

was written for the first and only ever checked that the job was ALIVE. It
never checked it was CURRENT. That hole is now closed.

working tree. The first cut used `find -newer src/` and would have failed
the gate on any unfinished edit — blocking the gate that tells you whether
the edit is good. A dirty tree is ordinary; a deployed binary behind
committed code is the defect.

title: The OIDC canary tests a local authority, not production — which is why a broken auth.notme.bot went unnoticed
description:
Correction to a claim I put in docs/release/goal-zero-promotion.md, exposed by the rc.1 failure (signet-ddb0f3).

The plan repeatedly credits .github/workflows/oidc-signing.yml as "the continuous live-authority canary" and treats its green status as evidence that the authority contract is healthy — §1 findings, the §4 compatibility matrix row, and the Phase 1 entry criteria all lean on it.

That is wrong. oidc-signing.yml spawns a LOCAL Go authority and points the CLI at it: `./signet authority exchange-github-token --authority-url http://localhost:8080 --auto`, with provider config `audience: http://localhost:8080` (:59-95). It never contacts https://auth.notme.bot. It proves the Go authority's exchange logic works against itself — real coverage, but not of production.

The consequence was demonstrated rather than theorised: oidc-signing.yml was green on the exact commit rc.1 was cut from, while production /cert/gha was returning HTTP 401 on every enrollment (notme-718ac0). A canary that cannot see the thing it is watching reported healthy right up to the failure.

FIX — and prefer the honest cheap one over the impressive expensive one:
1. Immediately: correct the plan's language so no phase's entry criteria rest on this job as evidence about production. It is a Go-authority regression test, and should be named that.
2. Then decide whether a real production canary is wanted. It is not free: it would mint a real certificate from the production CA on a schedule, which is issuance volume and log noise for a liveness check. A cheaper 80% is an unauthenticated GET of /.well-known/signet-authority.json plus a deliberately malformed POST to /cert/gha asserting a 4xx SHAPE rather than a 500 — that would have caught this exact outage, since the failure mode was a 401 with a crypto error rather than the expected rejection.
3. Whatever is chosen, Phase 1's entry criteria must name a check that actually touches the authority the release will sign against.

comments.text:
Reinforced from the notme side, and their version of the finding is sharper than mine — worth folding into whatever this bead produces.

My finding: signet's oidc-signing.yml canary tests a LOCAL Go authority at localhost:8080, never auth.notme.bot, so it reported healthy while production was returning 401 on every enrollment.

Their finding, validating the same deploy: with a 10/90 version split confirmed live, 85 sampled requests ALL hit the old version — 0.9^85 is about 0.01%. So verifying during a soak by sampling is not merely weak evidence about the new version; it can be NO evidence. They ruled out caching (the cache key preserves the query, so every request reached the Worker). Pinning via Cloudflare-Workers-Version-Overrides is how they actually validated 12/12 against the new version before promoting.

And the trap underneath it, which generalises past Workers: they first tried to distinguish versions by the JWKS kid, since main computes a 128-bit kid where the deployed version predated that. Pinned to the NEW version the kid was still 8 hex — because it is Durable Object state written at key creation, not recomputed per request. A canary's distinguishing signal must come from the code path under test, never from persisted state, or it passes identically on both versions and "confirms" on evidence that could not have shown otherwise.

Both findings are the same failure in different clothing: a check that cannot observe the thing it claims to be checking. Mine watched the wrong host; theirs sampled a distribution that made the new version nearly unobservable, using a signal that would not have distinguished the versions anyway.

Implication for this bead's fix: whatever production check replaces the current claim must (a) contact the authority the release actually signs against, and (b) assert on something computed per-request by the code under test. Tracked on their side as notme-325916.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: The promotion plan no longer cites oidc-signing.yml as evidence about the production authority, and Phase 1's entry criteria name a check that actually contacts the authority the release signs against; if a production canary is added, it is documented what it costs in issuance volume.

title: GHA OIDC → bridge cert → full signing flow in CI
description:
## Problem

The `/exchange-token` endpoint verifies GHA OIDC tokens and maps capabilities, but the actual bridge certificate minting is still TODO (authority.go:1097-1108). This means the full flow — ambient GHA OIDC identity → bridge cert → artifact/commit signing — cannot be exercised end-to-end in CI yet.

## What Exists

- `pkg/oidc/` — full GitHubActionsProvider with token verification, claim extraction, capability mapping
- `cmd/signet/authority.go` — authority server with `/exchange-token` endpoint (token exchange works, cert minting is stubbed)
- `docs/examples/github-actions-workflow.yml` — example workflow (references `signet authority exchange-github-token` which doesn't exist yet)
- `docs/design/004-bridge-certs.md` — design for bridge certificates with capability attestation
- `pkg/attest/x509/` — LocalCA that can issue certs

## What's Missing

1. **Bridge cert minting in `/exchange-token`** — wire up `authority.mintClientCertificate` (or a new `mintBridgeCertificate`) to actually produce a cert with capabilities embedded as X.509 extensions
2. **CLI command for token exchange** — `signet authority exchange-github-token` referenced in the example workflow
3. **Integration test in GHA** — a real workflow that exercises the full flow using ambient OIDC credentials

## Relationship to Middleware (signet-4jn)

Once bridge certs are being minted from GHA OIDC, they can be used with signet's HTTP middleware (`pkg/http/middleware/`) to authenticate requests. This is the same middleware that signet-4jn proposes wrapping around MCP transports. The chain: GHA OIDC → bridge cert → sign HTTP requests → middleware validates.

## Why This Matters

GHA OIDC is the most practical path to "signet in the cloud" — no secrets to manage, ambient identity from the CI platform, short-lived certs that match signet's security model.

title: CI: short-SHA reference in workflow breaks every PR + main run
description:
## Problem
A workflow in `.github/workflows/` references `agentic-research/notme@2c540af` — a 7-character SHA. GitHub Actions no longer accepts short SHAs and rejects the workflow with:

```
Unable to resolve action `agentic-research/notme@2c540af`, the provided ref `2c540af` is the shortened version of a commit SHA, which is not supported. Please use the full commit SHA `2c540af08cdb2f3abd4497221bb6741d33fc82f9` instead.
```

This fails the "Acquire bridge cert / OIDC Exchange" check on every PR (verified on signet #124 and the last 5 main commits). Pre-existing — not introduced by any one PR — but blocks merging PRs that have rulesets requiring it.

## Acceptance criteria
- The failing workflow file's `uses: agentic-research/notme@<short-sha>` line replaced with the full 40-char SHA
- (Optional) Add a pre-commit hook or CI lint that catches short-SHA action references at write time (similar to the `lint-doc-counts.mjs` pattern in cloister)
- Workflow run succeeds on a test PR
- Recent main commits' "Acquire bridge cert / OIDC Exchange" checks go green after the fix

## Inputs
- `.github/workflows/` — find the file with `uses: agentic-research/notme@2c540af`
- The full SHA per the GH Actions error message: `2c540af08cdb2f3abd4497221bb6741d33fc82f9`

## Output shape
PR against signet. Single-line fix in one workflow file. Net diff: 1 line changed.

## Scope boundary
Just this one short-SHA reference. A repo-wide audit for other short-SHA pins is a follow-up bead.

## Failure mode
PR's CI shows "Acquire bridge cert / OIDC Exchange" still failing with the same error message.

## Time-box
S (1 line change + test PR)

## Why this matters
This check is required by signet's branch protection / ruleset — every PR is currently blocked on a workflow that cannot succeed because of stale reference syntax. Detected during PR #124's CI run (substrate-IDL L10+L11 Copilot-review fixes). Discovered via `rosary-99f891`-class drift (the workflow was written when short-SHA worked; the GH platform behavior changed underneath).

## Related
