title: Enforce SCT presence at signet's verifier — the mechanism that makes notme's CT log complete (not just --ctfe config)
description:
Blocked on notme-907299 (notme must run the log and embed SCTs first). Filing now because the signet-side change is small, already measured, and should not be rediscovered later.

CURRENT STATE. cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact.go builds a cosign trusted root treating the notme authority as the Fulcio-equivalent:

  cosign trusted-root create --with-default-services --no-default-ctfe \
    --fulcio=url=<authorityURL>,certificate-chain=<caPath> --out trusted-root.json

The `--no-default-ctfe` flag is there for a stated reason (sign_artifact.go:161): "Notme/Cloister does not issue RFC 6962 SCTs. Keep public Rekor and TSA verification material, but do not advertise CTFE for this CA." That is correct today — it opts out of certificate transparency because notme cannot supply it. It is also the ONLY thing standing between signet and full CT-covered verification.

THE CHANGE, verified against cosign v3.1.1 locally: `cosign trusted-root create --ctfe` accepts the SAME key-value shape as the `--fulcio` flag this code already passes — required keys url, public-key (path to a PEM public key), start-time; optional end-time and origin. So:

  --no-default-ctfe   →   --ctfe=url=<notme-ct-log>,public-key=<ctlog.pub>,start-time=<...>,origin=<...>

The optional `origin` key is the tiled-log checkpoint identity, i.e. cosign already anticipates Static CT logs in a custom trusted root. This matters because notme is targeting the STATIC CT API, not RFC 6962 — RFC 6962 logs went read-only 2025-11-30 and shut down 2026-02-28 (letsencrypt.org/2025/08/14/rfc-6962-logs-eol).

SECOND, SMALLER PIECE: enroll.go already writes the authority CA bundle to disk for the trusted root (enrolled.CABundlePEM → <artifact>.signet.ca.pem). The log's public key needs the same treatment — fetched during enrolment and written alongside — so trusted-root construction has a local path to hand `--ctfe`.

NOTHING ELSE MOVES. The KMS plugin (kms.SignerVerifier over the official cliplugin handler), the Ed25519ph digest handling, the enrolment flow and the trusted-root construction are all already correct and exercised.

ACCEPTANCE — the negative control is the point, not the happy path: `cosign verify` must PASS against a notme-issued artifact with CT verification enabled, AND a certificate carrying no valid SCT must be REJECTED. A verification that only ever passes proves nothing; the existing image-signing path is credible precisely because a wrong-workflow identity is rejected (verified live 2026-08-05).

CROSS-REPO: notme-907299 (notme runs the log, embeds SCTs, anchors tree heads), cloister-ad4eac / cloister-ad7b5a (monitor the anchored heads; mirror tiles for offline verification). notme-8e8836 is the shared out-of-band-anchor premise.

comments.text:
Scope correction, measured on main (010a05e): the change is FIVE sites, not two, and one of the missing three makes this bead's own acceptance criteria unachievable as currently scoped.

Full inventory of SCT-related flags in signet:

1. cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact.go:163 — `--no-default-ctfe` in createCosignTrustedRoot. In the bead. ✔
2. cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact.go:205 — **`--insecure-ignore-sct` in cosignVerifyBlobArgs. NOT in the bead, and it is the blocking one.** While this flag is present, cosign verify-blob ignores SCTs entirely — so the AC's negative control ("a certificate carrying no valid SCT must be REJECTED") cannot fail-as-required no matter what the trusted root says. Configuring `--ctfe` without removing this yields a green test that proves nothing: CT material is declared and never enforced. This is the same shape as the release-signing path being "merged but unproven" — a gate that exists in configuration but not in effect.
3. cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact_test.go:53,78,97 — the existing tests pin all three flag strings as exact args. They will fail on the change and must be updated in the same commit; they are also where the negative control belongs.
4. scripts/release/verify_release.sh:171,192 — the release verification gate (added under signet-cf2adc) independently builds its own cosign trusted root with `--no-default-ctfe` and verifies with `--insecure-ignore-sct`. This is the clean-machine gate that decides whether a published release is promotable. If it is not updated with the rest, every release continues to be verified with CT disabled AFTER the log is live — the verification would keep passing while silently checking less than it claims. It also has a `--ca-bundle` escape hatch for CA rotation that will need a log-key equivalent.
5. .github/actions/sign-artifact/README.md:43,51 — documents both flags; stale docs here mislead the next implementer into reproducing the old invocation.

Suggested files update: add scripts/release/verify_release.sh, cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact_test.go, and .github/actions/sign-artifact/README.md to the bead's file scope so parallel-dispatch overlap detection sees them and so nobody ships item 1 alone.

Suggested AC addition: the negative control must be shown to FAIL BEFORE the fix (a cert without an SCT passing under `--insecure-ignore-sct`) and pass after — otherwise the test cannot distinguish "CT enforced" from "flag removed but log misconfigured, and cosign fell back to accepting".

Nothing here changes the blocked-on-notme-907299 status; it is all signet-side work that lands in one commit once the log is running.

comments.text:
Blocked status re-verified empirically 2026-08-05, so the next person does not re-probe:

- GET https://auth.notme.bot/.well-known/signet-authority.json → 200, and its key set contains NO ct/log entry of any kind: algorithms_supported, ca_bundle_endpoint, cert_endpoint, cert_gha_endpoint, cert_types_supported, documentation, dpop_signing_alg_values_supported, grant_types_supported, issuer, jwks_uri, token_endpoint. The authority does not advertise a log.
- /ct/v1/get-sth and /.well-known/ct → 500 (that is the VPC fallthrough to the dead Fly upstream documented in signet-c0a318, not a log returning an error).
- notme-907299 is open, P1, design — the log is not built, let alone running.

Why nothing here can be started rather than merely "should not be": the change needs two values that do not exist yet. `--ctfe` requires url + public-key + start-time (cosign v3.1.1 key-value shape, same as --fulcio), and there is no log to supply them. And `--insecure-ignore-sct` cannot be dropped ahead of the log either — certificates carry no SCTs today, so removing it makes verification fail closed on EVERY artifact, breaking release signing outright. The two flags must move together, after the log, or not at all. Same for enroll.go writing the log public key: there is no key.

What was done in the meantime (PR #161, merged as 4b11c76): all five sites now carry `SCT SITE n of 5` markers pointing at this bead, so the coupling is discoverable from whichever file someone opens first — the failure mode this guards against is changing the Go side and missing scripts/release/verify_release.sh, which builds its own cosign trusted root in a different language and would keep verifying every release with CT disabled while printing PASS.

One design note for whoever implements it. The five-site spread exists because verify_release.sh RE-IMPLEMENTS the trusted-root construction rather than invoking the Go binary's. If that duplication is collapsed — either by having the script call a `sigstore-kms-signet trusted-root` subcommand, or by both reading one declarative flag source — the CT change becomes a single edit and this class of drift stops recurring. That refactor is unblocked TODAY and does not depend on the log; it is deliberately not folded into this bead because it changes the release gate's dependency surface (a clean-machine verifier would then need the Go binary, not just cosign), which is a trade worth deciding on its own merits rather than as a side effect.

comments.text:
Relevant to how this bead gets framed, and to what signet's release notes may claim.

Measured with cosign v3.1.1 using signet's exact invocation (`cosign trusted-root create --with-default-services --no-default-ctfe`): the generated trusted root contains tlogs = 2 (rekor.sigstore.dev, log2025-1.rekor.sigstore.dev), ctlogs = 0, timestampAuthorities = 1. So `--no-default-ctfe` strips ONLY the CT material — Rekor inclusion is still required by the trusted root that both the signer and scripts/release/verify_release.sh verify against. The comment at sign_artifact.go:210 ("Rekor inclusion remains required by the generated trusted root") is accurate.

Combined with cosignSignBlobArgs passing `--certificate` and `--certificate-chain` into sign-blob, this means signet's signed artifacts already put the bridge cert into a public, third-party, append-only log at signing time. Signet's transparency posture on the release path is therefore materially better than "no CT log" implies, and the release notes may say so — as long as they are precise about the distinction:

- WHAT IS TRUE TODAY: every signed artifact's signature and signing certificate are recorded in public Rekor, verifiable by anyone, in a log signet's own org does not operate.
- WHAT IS NOT TRUE UNTIL THIS BEAD LANDS: certificates carry an embedded SCT, so the transparency proof does NOT travel with the credential — it travels with the signature bundle. An offline or air-gapped verifier holding only a certificate cannot check that the cert was ever logged. And issuance itself is unlogged: a cert minted and never used to sign appears nowhere.

That distinction is exactly what `--insecure-ignore-sct` encodes today, and it is why the flag is correct rather than merely tolerated at this stage.

Filed the fuller analysis on notme-907299, including why submitting to an EXISTING public CT log is not an option (public logs enforce accepted-roots policy; a private CA's chain is rejected at submission), and why Rekor covers only the signing path — /cert, /cert/passkey and /token produce no Rekor entry, so that bead's "every grant path is covered" claim needs revisiting.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Retitled and raised P2 → P1 after the notme side corrected my analysis. The change is in what this bead IS, not in its scope or its blocked status.

I had framed this as configuration — swap a cosign flag once a log exists. That undersells it. CT's value is not that certificates appear in a log; it is that verifiers REQUIRE an SCT, so a certificate lacking one is unusable. That requirement is what makes a log COMPLETE rather than a sample. Without it, a log records only the certs that happened to be used, and an issued-but-unused cert is invisible with nothing rejecting it.

The enforcement point for notme-issued certificates is signet, because signet is their primary verifier. `--insecure-ignore-sct` at cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact.go:205 and scripts/release/verify_release.sh:192 is literally the switch that disables the requirement. So this bead is the enforcement half of notme-907299 — the thing that converts notme's log from a record into a requirement — not the tidy-up that follows it.

Two consequences worth carrying forward:

1. The existing acceptance criteria were already right for the wrong reason. "A certificate carrying no valid SCT must be REJECTED" is not a nice-to-have negative test; it is the entire mechanism. The requirement that it be demonstrated FAILING before the fix (added earlier) matters even more under this framing, since a vacuously-passing negative control would mean the log is a record nobody enforces.

2. Ordering with notme-907299 is genuinely two-sided, not strictly downstream. notme must run the log and embed SCTs before signet can enforce; but until signet enforces, notme's log provides sampling rather than completeness, so neither half delivers the property alone. Worth stating in whichever bead gets picked up first so it is not treated as "ship the log, then optionally wire the flag later".

Still blocked on notme-907299 — no log, no key, and dropping --insecure-ignore-sct ahead of SCTs would fail-closed on every artifact.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
TWO THINGS FROM RECENT GITSIGN RELEASES worth folding in when this bead is picked up, since signet's KMS plugin explicitly bridges "Sigstore tools (cosign, gitsign)".

1. REKOR v2 / TILES. gitsign v0.17.0 (2026-07-29) added "Rekor v2 (rekor-tiles) signing support" plus an experimental sigstore-go client and online Rekor flows. Combined with Let's Encrypt retiring RFC 6962 logs (shut down 2026-02-28) in favour of the Static CT API, the tiled-log shift is now visible on BOTH the CT and Rekor sides. That is why notme-907299 targets Static CT rather than RFC 6962, and it means the `--ctfe` change this bead describes should assume a TILED log — cosign v3.1.1's `--ctfe` already accepts the optional `origin` key, which is the tiled checkpoint identity.

2. BUNDLE FORMAT. gitsign v0.15.1 migrated its release signing to the COSIGN v3 BUNDLE FORMAT. signet's sign_artifact.go already passes `--bundle`, and cosign v3.1.1 is what is installed locally — but worth CONFIRMING signet emits the v3 bundle shape rather than a legacy one when this work happens, because the bundle is where the Rekor inclusion proof rides. That matters directly for notme's offline story: the proof travels in the bundle, not in the certificate, so an air-gapped verifier depends on the bundle carrying it (cloister-ad7b5a).

NOT A CHANGE OF SCOPE for this bead — it is still "replace --no-default-ctfe with --ctfe=..." plus writing the log's public key alongside the CA bundle in enroll.go. These are constraints on the shape of the value, not extra work.

Also relevant to signet generally, though outside this bead: gitsign v0.16.0 (2026-05-06) fixed "gitsign verify accepts signatures over go-git-normalized bytes" — a verifier accepting a signature computed over a NORMALIZED form rather than the exact signed bytes. I checked notme's side: AuthService.sign() signs the payload exactly as given, with no normalization, and notme does not verify git commits — so notme is not exposed to that class. title: chore(sign): drop rs/crates/sign fork, depend on LLO's leyline-sign
description:
Signet-side of `ley-line-open-d4fdf4`. Delete signet's leyline-sign fork; consume LLO's canonical version instead.

## Findings

Overlap detector 2026-07-09 confirmed `signet/rs/crates/sign/` is a stale fork of LLO's `leyline-sign`:
- `cert.rs`, `oid.rs` — md5 IDENTICAL to LLO's copies
- `cms.rs` — older subset; adds `signingTime` attribute (LLO deliberately omits for wasm32 time-source portability)
- `ffi.rs` — LLO's copy adds wasm32 allocator exports
- `lib.rs`, `error.rs` — LLO adds cert_chain.rs (901 LoC), bin/helper.rs, host/ (ADR-0019)

Per README (`rs/crates/sign/README.md` ~L9): "Prepared — not yet integrated. Cloudflare Workers currently use `@peculiar/x509` in TypeScript." No Go callers of `signet-sign` (grep on pkg/ finds no imports).

## What ships

### 1. Delete `rs/crates/sign/` entirely

Direct analog of cloister PR #119 (bead `cloister-8f4d3f`, merged 2026-07-09).

### 2. Decide `signingTime` reconciliation

Signet's cms.rs adds signingTime; LLO's omits it. Two paths:

- **A**: LLO adds an optional `signing-time` feature to its leyline-sign; signet consumers enable it if needed. Requires an LLO PR first; then signet's future consumers set `features = ["signing-time"]`.
- **B**: Accept the drop. No signet-issued CMS blobs are in production per README, so no wire compat concern today.

Recommend **B** for this PR since no production consumer exists. If a future signet CMS consumer needs signingTime, refile as path A.

### 3. If signet's Rust workspace becomes empty

`rs/Cargo.toml`'s `members` list drops to zero. Options:
- Delete the whole `rs/` directory (it becomes vestigial)
- Move to `rs.retired/` with a README explaining
- Leave the workspace empty as a placeholder for future Rust work

Agent decides based on whether anything else in signet references the workspace.

### 4. Taskfile cleanup

Remove any `rs:sign:*` targets that referenced the deleted crate.

### 5. Docs update

If any signet docs reference the local crate path, update to point at LLO's `leyline-sign` (git dep or, later, published wasm artifact via LLO bead `ley-line-open-a2099a`).

## Rules

- Commit prefix `[<this-bead-id>]` (Golden Rule 11)
- Signet's local gate (`task check` or equivalent) must be green
- Verify NO Go code imports break (`grep -rn "signet-sign" pkg/`)
- Working copy: `~/remotes/art/signet` (per overlap agent, `~/github/art/signet` and `~/remotes/art/signet` are identical trees)

## Non-goals

- **NO changes to signet's Go tree** (pkg/*, SIG1/COSE, ML-DSA-44 — all genuinely distinct scope)
- **NO wasm-consumer wiring** — that waits on LLO bead `a2099a` (wasm publish infra)
- **NO signingTime feature-gate in LLO** unless path A is chosen (this PR chooses B)

## Related

- `ley-line-open-d4fdf4` — LLO-side tracking + rationale
- `ley-line-open-7226e3` / `cloister-8f4d3f` — cloister analog (reference implementation)
- `ley-line-open-a2099a` — wasm publish infra (blocks future signet-uses-LLO-wasm)

## Provenance

- Overlap detector 2026-07-09
- Cloister consolidation PR #160 landed same day (2026-07-09)

comments.text:
rc.1 CUT AND BURNED — the rehearsal did its job on the first run.

Tag v0.3.0-rc.1 pushed at 18a93832b36f8e29d51aff649d63c37baa9b208b (main, green on CI Tests + OIDC Signing E2E + Claude Code Review). Release run: https://github.com/agentic-research/signet/actions/runs/31063287702

RESULT: all three build jobs SUCCEEDED (darwin-arm64, linux-amd64, linux-arm64). The "Sign + verify release artifacts" step FAILED. No release was published — `gh release view v0.3.0-rc.1` returns "release not found" — because release.yml signs and verifies BEFORE creating the release. The fail-closed ordering worked exactly as designed: a broken signing path produced no artifacts rather than unsigned ones.

THE ERROR, verbatim:
  sigstore-kms-signet: certificate exchange failed (HTTP 401):
  {"error":"P-256 proof verification error: Requested algorithm \"ECDSA\" does not match this CryptoKey's algorithm \"Ed25519\"."}

ROOT CAUSE — traced to origin, not just the emitter. Signet's side is correct: cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/enroll.go generates a P-256 ECDSA key for mTLS (:95) and an Ed25519 key for signing (:101), signs the binding with ECDSA over the P-256 key (:131), and POSTs both keys explicitly role-labelled (public_keys.mtls / public_keys.signing, proofs.mtls / proofs.signing). The request is unambiguous.

The failure originates in notme's Worker. worker.ts:742 verifies proofs.mtls with {name:"ECDSA"} against mtlsPubKey, and the error text matches worker.ts:750 exactly, so that is the deployed path. mtlsPubKey came back as an Ed25519 CryptoKey, meaning importPublicKey mis-detected signet's P-256 SPKI.

AND THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN AND MERGED — just not deployed. notme's worker/src/cert-authority.ts:123-178 now dispatches on the SPKI's own algorithm OID (isEd25519Spki), and its comment describes our exact symptom: "WAS 'try Ed25519, fall back to ECDSA P-256 on throw'. That is broken on workerd: an Ed25519 import of a P-256 SPKI SUCCEEDS rather than throwing, so the fallback never ran and every key came back as {name:'Ed25519'}." That commit (ddd5f98, "plus a P-256 PoP bug that broke every cert route") IS an ancestor of notme's origin/main. So notme's main is correct and PRODUCTION IS STALE.

DISPOSITION per the plan: rc.1 is burned — not deleted, not moved, not promoted. rc.2 follows once notme deploys. Nothing about signet needs to change; this is not a fix-forward on our code.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
rc.2 CUT AND BURNED — the deploy fixed the first bug and revealed a second one underneath it.

Tag v0.3.0-rc.2 at the same tree as rc.1 (18a9383) — no signet change was needed or made. Run: https://github.com/agentic-research/signet/actions/runs/31065683262. Builds all green; Sign + verify failed again; no release published.

THE ERROR CHANGED, and that change is the evidence notme's deploy worked:
  rc.1: "P-256 proof verification error: Requested algorithm ECDSA does not match this CryptoKey's algorithm Ed25519"  — the key import threw
  rc.2: "P-256 proof-of-possession failed"                                                                             — import fine, verify RAN and returned false

So notme-718ac0 is genuinely resolved. What it was hiding is a second defect in the same handler: with the stale deploy, the import threw before verify could execute, so nobody could observe that verify would also fail.

ROOT CAUSE, reproduced rather than argued (filed as notme-a011d2, P0). WebCrypto's subtle.verify({name:"ECDSA", hash:"SHA-256"}, ...) hashes its data argument. The Worker passes bindingPayload, which is ALREADY SHA-256(bindingInput) — so it checks the signature against SHA-256(SHA-256(bindingInput)). Go's ecdsa.Sign treats its input as a finished digest, so enroll.go:131 signs SHA-256(bindingInput). One hash versus two.

Proof: generated a signet-shaped proof in Go, verified it under Node's WebCrypto both ways —
  verify(data = binding digest)    [as deployed]  : false
  verify(data = binding pre-image) [proposed fix] : true

Only the P-256 proof is affected. The Ed25519 proof in the same request succeeds because WebCrypto Ed25519 is PureEdDSA and does not pre-hash, so both sides operate on `binding` and agree. The two verification blocks read as symmetric and are not — which is why this survived review.

Fix is one argument on notme's side (pass bindingInput, not bindingPayload). Signet's construction is the conventional Go one and should not change.

DISPOSITION: rc.2 burned — not deleted, not moved. Two rc tags now stand as the record of two distinct authority defects, which is what a disposable rehearsal channel is for. rc.3 follows notme-a011d2.

Also worth stating plainly: signet has still never successfully signed a release. Every failure so far has been outside signet, but the path remains unproven, and the burn count is now the honest measure of how unproven it was.

The Create Release job — the one that does the signing — has now sat QUEUED for over 20 minutes with no runner assigned and no steps started, on plain ubuntu-latest, despite the build jobs on the same label having completed minutes earlier.

comments.text:
rc.3 STILL PENDING — GitHub Actions capacity, degrading rather than recovering.

Attempt 1 (run 31126879330, dispatched): all three builds SUCCEEDED, then Create Release sat queued with no runner and was ultimately CANCELLED. The signing step never executed.
Attempt 2 (run 31127371833, re-dispatched): now even the BUILD jobs are queued. Worse than attempt 1, which at least got build runners.

Neither run reached the authority, so both say NOTHING about notme-a011d2. rc.3 remains not-burned: a tag is burned when its signing step runs and fails, and this one has never run.

Two independent blockers now stand between here and a signed release, and only one is anybody's fault:
1. GitHub Actions is not scheduling jobs for this repo. Outside our control; nothing to fix on our side.
2. notme's double-hash fix is still absent from their origin/main. Since their deploys are manual the tree does not settle what is deployed, but there is no positive evidence it is fixed either.

WHAT I DID WITH THE WAIT, because "CI is down" should not also mean "the release path is unknowable": the release workflow inlined its go build and sha256sum, so none of it could be run anywhere but inside a runner. `task verify-release TAG=v0.3.0-rc.4` **PASS**: 4 artifacts, checksums and signature bundles verified against a trust anchor fetched independently from `https://auth.notme.bot/.well-known/ca-bundle.pem`. All four signed as `URI:wimse://notme.bot/gha/agentic-research/signet`. The rehearsal took four tags and found four distinct defects, **none in signet's own code** — which is what a disposable rehearsal channel is for:

| Tag | Failure | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| rc.1 | notme production 8 days stale; `importPublicKey` mis-detected a P-256 SPKI as Ed25519 | notme |
| rc.2 | WebCrypto double-hash — `subtle.verify` hashes its data argument, Go's `ecdsa.Sign` does not (notme-a011d2, fixed + deployed) | notme |
| rc.3 | GitHub Actions incident: tag push did not trigger; dispatch queued then cancelled | GitHub |
| rc.3 | publish-before-upload against immutable releases — release sealed empty, unrecoverable | signet workflow (#170) |
| rc.4 | — | — |

## The rc.3 cause is now established, and it was mine

I previously said I could not tell whether the tag-immutability ruleset caused it. The evidence now settles it:

- `v0.2.1` (published 2026-03-22, long before): `isImmutable=false`
- `immutable-tags` ruleset created 2026-08-06 19:54 UTC
- `v0.3.0-rc.3` (published 2026-08-06 22:58 UTC, first release cut after): `isImmutable=true`

Protecting tags makes GitHub treat releases on those tags as immutable. There is no repo-level setting that reveals this — `gh api repos/O/R --jq .immutable_releases` returns `null` either way; only `gh release view <tag> --json isImmutable` shows it. So enabling tag immutability is what turned a latent workflow ordering bug into permanent loss of a release.

`v0.3.0-rc.3` remains published, empty, and unrepairable. Left as-is deliberately: it is honest evidence of the failure, and the tag cannot be recut anyway.

## Blast radius beyond signet

The earlier org audit reported "zero unsafe" — that verdict was measured against the wrong criteria (floating-major-tag and Action-repo breakage only). Re-audited all 13 public non-fork repos with a publish-ordering check added:

- `mache` — `release.yml` publishes with no `draft: true` → **mache-9ba2ed** (P1)
- `rosary` — same → **rosary-9bd1de** (P1)
- `notme` — publishes a reusable workflow (`workflow_call` in `gha-identity.yml`); separate hazard, unchanged verdict

Both would have been destroyed the same way had tag protection been enabled first. The standalone `gh-immutable-tags.sh` now refuses on this pattern rather than warning, since the damage it prevents is not recoverable.

Phase 1 exit criteria met. Phase 2 (`signet-ddd7d7`) is unblocked; PR #171 adds the per-tag release notes v0.3.0 needs before it is cut.

## Phase 2 started — v0.3.0 published and verified 2026-08-07

`v0.3.0` at commit `e64ad9e`: 20 assets, `prerelease: true`, not latest, `isImmutable: true`.

`task verify-release TAG=v0.3.0` **PASS** — 4 artifacts, checksums and signature bundles verified against a trust anchor fetched independently from `https://auth.notme.bot/.well-known/ca-bundle.pem`, all signed as `URI:wimse://notme.bot/gha/agentic-research/signet`.

**Soak clock starts today.** ≥5 working days → earliest Phase 3 date **2026-08-14**. Exit needs zero release-attributable P0/P1 filed during soak and oidc-signing green throughout. Promotion (`signet-de0589`) stays an explicit human step.

## Release notes carry the honesty §4 required

Added a per-tag notes mechanism (#171) because generated notes structurally cannot say this — they summarize merged PRs, and an endpoint that was never served here produced no PR to summarize. `docs/release/notes/<TAG>.md` when present, generated-only when absent; per-tag rather than a workflow constant so a caveat cannot outlive the defect it describes.

Re-probed rather than copied from the plan: `POST /exchange-token` and `POST /api/cert/register` both return **404** — removed, not the 500/CF-1101 the plan recorded — and discovery advertises only `github_actions_oidc`+`dpop`. The notes also state what the signatures do *not* prove, given `notme-191328` (rate limiters declared but unbound) and `notme-2c4209` (CA registration effectively open).

## I deviated from the plan's letter, and the plan was wrong

Phase 2 said cut `v0.3.0` on the same commit as the passing rc. I cut one commit later (rc.4 = `234efc3`, v0.3.0 = `e64ad9e`) because the release-notes PR landed between. I predicted the binaries would be identical since the diff is only `docs/` and `.github/`. **They are not** — all three hash differently.

Cause: Go stamps `vcs.revision`, `vcs.time`, `vcs.modified` into every binary via `debug.BuildInfo`, and `-trimpath` does not suppress them. Any commit that moves the tag changes every SHA-256.

Proven, not assumed — rebuilt at both commits with `-buildvcs=false`:

```
8628f362b2aded49adc8d6e43371f2cd51adca69a4240f34a68ac6631d3c81c2  rc4.bin
8628f362b2aded49adc8d6e43371f2cd51adca69a4240f34a68ac6631d3c81c2  final.bin
IDENTICAL
```

So no code moved between rc.4 and v0.3.0, and "same commit as the rc" was neither necessary nor sufficient as a check. PR #172 corrects the plan and documents the reproduction that actually proves the property.

title: APAS v0.4.0: predicate becomes a referenced profile, not a requirement — align with in-toto's own layering
description:
Two findings from examining Chainguard's DriftlessAF (chainguard.dev/driftlessaf) as the first realistic second implementer of APAS. Both are v0.4.0-shaped changes to a document just shipped at v0.3.0, filed now because the evidence is fresh.

FINDING 1 — THE PREDICATE SHOULD BE A PROFILE, AND IN-TOTO ALREADY PROVES IT.

APAS §3.1/§3.2 mandates predicateType https://notme.bot/provenance/dispatch/v1. in-toto — which APAS lists as a normative reference — does the opposite: the Statement is the standard, and predicates are pluggable, separately specified and separately versioned (SLSA provenance, SPDX and others are all independent predicate specs). So APAS mandating a single predicate URI is LESS standard-shaped than the standard it builds on. That is the strongest form of the argument: this is not loosening APAS, it is bringing it in line with its own normative reference.

Shape to adopt:
- APAS defines the PROPERTIES an attestation must carry — content-bound inputs, a fail-closed identity gate, a defined parent relationship, a signed envelope.
- predicateType becomes the PROFILE IDENTIFIER rather than a requirement.
- dispatch/v1 becomes one profile, referenced not mandated.
- A second profile shaped like an Envelope (below) could conform without pretending to have phases.

Side effect worth naming: this dissolves the notme.bot coupling entirely. v0.3.0 documented it as the one real coupling with a MUST-match-literally / MUST-NOT-dereference rule. Under profiles it stops being a caveat and becomes a non-issue, because no namespace is mandated at all.

FINDING 2 — A CORRECTION TO MY OWN v0.3.0-ERA CLAIM. I said DriftlessAF's execution model does not map to APAS phases. That was wrong, and it was wrong because I looked at the wrong layer.

agents/checkpoint is a suspend/resume primitive: an Envelope captures provider identity, config digest, turn budget, pending tool calls and the raw provider request; ValidateForResume gates the wake on version, provider, model and config digest, and the digest is REQUIRED so an empty one fails closed rather than vacuously matching (checkpoint/digest.go DigestJSON, ErrConfigDrift).

A suspend/resume boundary IS a phase boundary:
  APAS phase        <-> checkpoint Envelope
  handoff document  <-> Envelope
  chain_hash()      <-> ConfigDigest
  chain verification <-> ValidateForResume (fail-closed)

Both are a content-bound capture of execution state at a boundary that gates what happens next. The only difference is who the handoff addresses: APAS phases hand off between distinct roles; an Envelope hands off to the SAME executor after a pause. That is a narrower case of the same structure.

What I mistook for a mismatch was reconcilers/ and workqueue/ — level-triggered, retry-with-backoff, no phase sequence. But that is the SCHEDULING layer; agents/checkpoint is the agent-execution layer, which is what APAS describes. APAS never claimed to describe reconcilers.

So dispatch/v1 is less rosary-specific than I claimed. The phase concept survives; the assumption that does not is that phases are always BETWEEN DISTINCT AGENTS.

CONSTRAINT THE REWRITE MUST RESPECT: conformance has to keep meaning something. "Carry some predicate" is vacuous. The required properties must be testable, and the fail-closed rules are the load-bearing ones — note that signet (APAS §2.5 empty origin set yields origin-unknown, never origin-attested by vacuous truth) and Chainguard (empty config digest fails closed rather than vacuously matching) landed on the identical rule independently. Convergence like that is evidence the principle is real and the packaging is negotiable.

Also worth capturing while adjacent: Chainguard composed standards and invented nothing (CloudEvents for the trace envelope, sigstore for signing, checkpoint as a library primitive with no wire contract — DigestJSON's own doc concedes it is only as stable as encoding/json field ordering). Signet invented several formats. Some of that invention is load-bearing (offline verification, algorithm agility, PoP), some is not. A protocol earns its invention by being implementable by someone who did not write it, and this bead is the work that makes that true.

comments.text:
HOUSING QUESTION, raised alongside this work: should APAS continue to live inside the signet repo?

Concrete evidence the current arrangement is already straining, not a hypothetical: signet is at tag v0.3.0-rc.3 while APAS is at v0.3.0-draft. Same repository, same version string, two unrelated things. Someone reading "0.3.0" in this repo today cannot tell whether it means the CLI or the standard, and the two will keep diverging because they version on different clocks — APAS moves when the spec changes, signet when the software ships.

Industry precedent is uniform, and it is the precedent that matters if adoption is the goal. Every standard APAS would be compared against lives apart from its implementations, usually under a neutral foundation: SLSA (slsa-framework, OpenSSF), in-toto (CNCF), SPIFFE (CNCF), DSSE (secure-systems-lab), and sigstore's own protobuf-specs separately from cosign. Not one of them ships inside a single implementation's source tree.

The argument for co-location is real and should not be dismissed: a spec next to its reference implementation drifts less, because drift is visible in one diff — and this session repeatedly found signet docs asserting things the code did not do, caught precisely because both were in reach. A spec with no implementation is worse than one with a co-located implementation.

But the perception problem is the adoption problem. v0.3.0 fixed the LANGUAGE (roles, not product names, ~71 mentions down to 13). The LOCATION still says "this is signet's document". A prospective implementer does not clone an identity CLI to read a provenance standard.

Recommended sequencing, which makes this bead the prerequisite rather than a competing task:
1. Land this bead's profile work. It removes the last structural reason APAS must live near signet — once conformance is defined by properties and no namespace is mandated, nothing in the spec depends on signet's tree.
2. Fix the version collision, whichever way housing goes. At minimum APAS's version needs a distinguishable form so "0.3.0" is never ambiguous inside one repo.
3. Then decide housing on its merits. Moving is cheap AFTER (1) and expensive before it, because today the spec cites signet's own design docs as normative references and would take those citations with it.

Not proposing a move now. Proposing that this bead be understood as what makes a move possible later, and that the version collision be treated as a present defect rather than a future one.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
STRONGEST EVIDENCE PATH: build the second profile as a working demo rather than arguing for it on paper.

The bead currently makes a design argument — dispatch/v1 assumes phases between distinct agents, so a suspend/resume execution model cannot populate it honestly. That argument is correct but it is still an argument. A demo converts it into a demonstrated fact, and it is the difference between "we believe APAS is implementable by a second party" and "here is a conforming attestation produced by one."

Shape of the demo, using components that already exist rather than anything new:
- Take a checkpoint Envelope (provider identity, ConfigDigest, turn budget, pending tool calls, raw provider request).
- Wrap it in a DSSE envelope around an in-toto Statement — both already APAS normative references, and both already available in that ecosystem's dependency set (cosign v3, sigstore-go, protobuf-specs).
- Give it a predicateType that is NOT dispatch/v1. That is the point: an envelope-shaped profile identifier.
- Sign and verify with stock sigstore tooling.

What it would prove, and why each item matters more than the demo itself:
1. APAS conformance can be satisfied by a system with NO phases between distinct agents — the exact claim ded9d4 rests on.
2. The required-properties framing survives contact with a real second unit: ConfigDigest satisfies "content-bound inputs" where chain_hash() satisfies it for dispatch/v1. Same property, different mechanism, which is precisely what "profile" has to mean or the word is decoration.
3. The fail-closed rule holds across both — ValidateForResume refuses an empty digest rather than vacuously matching, exactly as §2.5 refuses an empty origin set. Two independent implementations enforcing the same rule is the strongest available argument that it belongs in the normative core rather than in one profile.

Sequencing note: the demo is worth MORE if built before the v0.4.0 rewrite than after. Built first, it tells us which properties are genuinely universal and which only looked universal because we had one implementation. Built after, it can only confirm choices already made — and would be liable to be shaped to fit them.

comments.text:
## Read the actual DriftlessAF source, not the GitHub summary — the integration is far smaller than assumed

Cloned `driftlessaf/go-driftlessaf` (`chainguard.dev/driftlessaf`, Go 1.26.4, Apache-2.0) and read the attestation and trace paths. My earlier assumption that an APAS L2 demo there would need signing infrastructure built is **wrong**, and correcting it changes what the demo costs.

### DriftlessAF already ships the entire APAS L2 substrate

`reconcilers/ocireconciler/statusmanager/` persists reconciler state as **signed OCI attestations** with Sigstore keyless:

- signing — `secant.AttestBundle` (`terraform-provider-cosign/pkg/private/secant`), Fulcio certs
- transparency — Rekor, incl. `cosign.SigningConfigRekorV2()`
- verification on read — `sigstore-go/pkg/verify`, full bundle verification, `WithExpectedIdentity`
- direct deps already include `sigstore/cosign/v3 v3.1.2`, `sigstore-go`, `protobuf-specs`, `in-toto/attestation v1.2.0`, `in-toto-golang v0.11.0`

So DSSE envelope, keyless identity, transparency log, and verify-on-read are **all present and in production use**. APAS contributes none of that.

### The seam is exactly one function argument

```go
stmt, err := secant.NewStatement(s.subject, bytes.NewReader(payload), s.manager.predicateType)
```

`predicateType` today is `https://statusmanager.chainguard.dev/{identity}` — a bespoke, identity-scoped type whose payload is `Status[T]{ObservedGeneration, Details}`, i.e. *reconciliation status*, not *agent provenance*. **That is the whole integration point.** An APAS predicate is a different `predicateType` string plus a different marshaled body through the same call. No new signing, no new verification, no new transport.

This is the strongest possible evidence for this bead's thesis: the one thing APAS should own is the thing DriftlessAF is missing, and the things APAS currently mandates are the things DriftlessAF already solved differently and correctly.

### The predicate body has a real source — two of them, and they disagree with dispatch/v1

`agents/agenttrace.Trace[T]` is the run record: `ID`, `OTelTraceID`, `InputPrompt`, `ToolCalls[]` (ID/Name/Params/Result/Error, plus `Recoverable` and `Terminal` flags), `Turns[] RecordedTurn` (per-turn model, token counts incl. cache reads, start/end, `Errors[]`, `Failed`), `Reasoning[]`, `AgentName`, `Model`, `Source`, `StartTime`/`EndTime`. `ExecutionContext` adds `ReconcilerKey`, `ReconcilerType`, `CommitSHA`, `TurnNumber`, `RequestID`.

That is richer than APAS dispatch/v1 assumes, and differently shaped: **the unit of work is a reconciler key reconciled to convergence, not a dispatch**. There is no dispatching *agent* to name as a distinct entity — which is precisely the L2 gap I flagged.

`agents/checkpoint` settles the phase question I got wrong earlier. `Envelope` carries `ReconcilerKey`, `RunID`, `Turn`, `RemainingTurns`, `Reason`, `PendingToolCalls[]`, `ProviderState`, and `ConfigDigest`. `ValidateForResume` is a **fail-closed gate**: schema version, provider, model, and config digest must all match, else `ErrConfigDrift` → rebuild from scratch. `DigestJSON` covers model params, tool definitions, and provider SDK version deliberately, so all drift funnels through one enforced check.

So a run legitimately **suspends and resumes across process boundaries**, and `RunID` — not the process — is what identifies it. An APAS model where a run is one continuous execution cannot describe this. The suspend/resume boundary is the phase-shaped thing, and `ConfigDigest` is already the exact "what could have changed under the pause" claim an attestation wants to bind. That is a genuine second profile with a real implementation behind it, satisfying this bead's acceptance criterion far better than one I'd invent.

### Consequence for sequencing

The demo is now clearly worth building **before** the v0.4.0 rewrite, and cheaply: no infrastructure, one predicate type and a mapping from `Trace` + `Envelope`. Built first it tells us which APAS properties are genuinely universal and which only looked universal because signet was the sole implementation. Two independent shapes — signet's dispatch and DriftlessAF's reconcile-to-convergence with suspend/resume — is the minimum to distinguish those.

One caveat to carry: DriftlessAF pins `sigstore-go` back to v1.2.2 (`replace`) because gitsign's `validatingRekorClient` does not satisfy v1.3.0's `sign.RekorClient` (sigstore/gitsign#861). A demo built against it inherits that pin.

title: P3: extract APAS spec to its own repo (apas-spec) when external implementations appear
description:
Trigger-based, not a current task.

## Current state

`signet/docs/apas/agent-provenance-standard.md` is the APAS spec, currently at v0.2.0-draft (committed 2026-05-09). It lives in signet because:

- signet IS the protocol authority for the cryptographic primitives APAS uses (CBOR canonical, Ed25519, sigid 4-entity model).
- Relative paths from `docs/apas/` to `signet/pkg/...` and `signet/docs/design/...` work natively.
- Single author, single primary consumer (notme), still draft status.

## When to extract

Extract to a dedicated `apas-spec` repo when ANY of these triggers fire:

1. **A second implementation appears** (Go-only, Rust-only, or external) and asks "where's the spec?"
2. **External auditors / partners** want a stable canonical URL for the standard.
3. **Versioned spec releases** become a need (independent of signet's release cadence).
4. **CycloneDX / in-toto / SLSA registries** want to link to APAS as an attestation-format peer.

None are true today.

## Migration plan (when triggered)

1. `git filter-branch` or `git subtree split` the `docs/apas/` history into a new repo `agentic-research/apas-spec`.
2. Move all internal references in signet, notme, rosary, ley-line-open from `signet/docs/apas/...` to `apas-spec/...`.
3. Add a stub `signet/docs/apas/README.md` redirecting to the new repo.
4. Update notme.bot's `/apas` page to render from the new repo.
5. Set up release tags (`v0.2.0`, etc.) on the new repo.
6. Optional: an `apas-spec` GitHub org or `agentic-research/apas` for community contributions.

## Anchors

- `signet/docs/apas/agent-provenance-standard.md` — current home (v0.2.0-draft)
- `signet/docs/apas/research.md` — sibling research doc
- `notme.bot/public/apas.html` — public face (eventually points at the spec repo)
- Conversation 2026-05-09 — extraction trigger discussion

description: Found during the Goal Zero release review (signet-cf2adc). go-cms main carries 7 unreleased commits (+2504/-65) beyond the v0.0.4 tag signet pins, including three verifier bypass fixes signet's CMS verification path (pkg/git/verify.go:134 cms.Verify) does not have: (1) SignedData.Version was unchecked — single-byte INTEGER tampering accepted, now constrained to {1,3,4,5} per RFC 5652 §5.1; (2) EncapContentInfo.eContentType unchecked on the no-signedAttributes path — OID bytes flippable without invalidating the signature, now must equal id-data per §11.1; (3) parseASN1Length accepted non-canonical DER lengths — malleability that breaks content-addressing over CMS blob hashes. title: release.yml: v0.3.0 (no hyphen) never actually publishes as a prerelease
description:
Found during adversarial review of the Goal Zero release promotion plan (docs/release/goal-zero-promotion.md, bead signet-cf2adc / PR #148).

.github/workflows/release.yml:125 sets `prerelease: ${{ contains(env.TAG, '-') }}`. The plan's Phase 2 (§2) requires tagging `v0.3.0` (no hyphen) and having it "published as prerelease (the beta channel)" for the soak, then flipped at Phase 3 via `gh release edit v0.3.0 --prerelease=false --latest`.

But `contains("v0.3.0", "-")` is false — there is no hyphen in "v0.3.0" — so release.yml will create it with `prerelease: false` from the very first Phase 2 run. It is never actually a GitHub prerelease during the 5-day soak; it's a normal (non-prerelease, just non-"latest") release visible to anyone browsing releases, undermining the "beta channel" framing the whole plan depends on. The plan's own §1 findings section correctly states only hyphenated tags become prereleases — directly contradicting §2 Phase 2's claim two sections later, and invalidating the Phase 3 rollback text "v0.3.0 stays prerelease forever" (it was never prerelease to begin with).

Secondary issue in the same diff: `make_latest: "false"` is unconditional (not just for the first release), so every future production tag (v0.3.1, v0.4.0, ...) will require the same manual `gh release edit --latest` step forever. The plan documents the manual flip only as a one-time "first signed release" asymmetry (§2 Phase 3, parenthetical "this asymmetry disappears after the first signed production release"), not as a permanent behavior now baked into the workflow.

Fix direction: either give the beta tag a real hyphenated form (e.g. v0.3.0-beta.1) promoted in place at Phase 3, or drop the prerelease-flag framing for Phase 2 and rely purely on the latest-pointer for soak isolation — and update the plan to state make_latest=false requires a manual flip on every future release, not only the first.

comments.text: Config-level fix on goal-zero/signet-release-plan (PR #148): release.yml now sets prerelease: true unconditionally (plus make_latest: "false"), replacing the hyphen rule — EVERY tag publishes as a GitHub prerelease and production status is always the explicit Phase 3 flip (gh release edit <tag> --prerelease=false --latest) after task verify-release passes. Plan §1/§2/§5 rewritten to match: the "Pre-release" badge is the channel marker, the soak is intentionally public, and the flip requirement is documented as permanent for all future releases (forgetting it leaves a loud, visible badge — not a silent state). The AC's first two clauses are satisfied; the final clause (gh api shows prerelease:true during soak) is runtime evidence that can only exist once the train runs — it will be captured by signet-ddb0f3 (first live confirmation on the rc) and signet-ddd7d7 (soak), so this bead is linked as a dependency of the soak bead and should close on that observation.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: release.yml's prerelease logic and the plan's Phase 2/3 text agree on what tag form actually publishes as a GitHub prerelease during soak; a maintainer can point to the exact tag pattern that makes v0.3.0 (or its replacement) a prerelease, and `gh api repos/agentic-research/signet/releases` on that tag shows prerelease:true during soak.

title: verify_release.sh: unanchored identity regexp + silent-pass on malformed checksums
description:
Found during adversarial review of the Goal Zero release promotion plan (docs/release/goal-zero-promotion.md, bead signet-cf2adc / PR #148), reviewing scripts/release/verify_release.sh committed in 2655404.

(a) Weaker identity check than the signing side it claims to mirror. Lines 140-141 use `--certificate-identity-regexp "$IDENTITY_REGEXP"` with default `IDENTITY_REGEXP="agentic-research/signet"` (no `^`/`$` anchors). The signing side (cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact.go:194-208, cosignVerifyBlobArgs) uses exact-match `--certificate-identity <identity>`, not a regex at all. An unanchored regex matches that substring anywhere in the certificate's SAN — any identity string that merely *contains* "agentic-research/signet" would also verify successfully. This contradicts the script's own header comment (lines 27-28): "mirrors cmd/sigstore-kms-signet/sign_artifact.go cosignVerifyBlobArgs." Fix: anchor the default (`^...$`) or switch to `--certificate-identity` with the exact expected identity string.

(b) Silent pass on malformed/empty checksums file. Lines 98-102 build the `artifacts` array purely by parsing `checksums-sha256.txt` with no assertion on the resulting count or the expected artifact set (the 4 known binaries + the checksums file itself). If that file is ever empty or its line format changes, the loop silently produces zero or too few entries, and the script still prints "PASS: ... N artifacts ... verified" for whatever small N it found instead of hard-failing. Fix: assert the parsed artifact count/set against an expected minimum before declaring PASS.

Neither issue is caught by any existing test — there is no test file for verify_release.sh and it isn't invoked from any CI workflow (confirmed via grep); it's a purely human-run gate, so these defects would only surface via a human's own vigilance, not a red build.

comments.text: Fixed on goal-zero/signet-release-plan (PR #148). (1) Identity: default regexp is now anchored — (^|[/:])agentic-research/signet([/:@.]|$) — so the repo path must appear as a path segment, and a new --identity flag does exact --certificate-identity matching for once the enrolled SAN shape is known from a real release; the header comment no longer claims to "mirror" cosignVerifyBlobArgs and instead documents the deliberate exact-vs-regexp relaxation. (2) Silent pass: the script now hard-fails when checksums-sha256.txt names fewer than 3 binaries (release.yml matrix floor) or any non-signet-* artifact name. Verified per the AC by manual runs with a gh shim serving a fixture release: truncated checksums (1 artifact, valid sha) → exit 1 "names only 1 artifacts"; empty checksums → exit 1 "names only 0 artifacts"; flag-shaped tag (--repo) rejected before any network call. Real-release regression check: v0.2.1 still passes checksums then hard-fails naming the four missing bundles. shellcheck clean.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: --certificate-identity-regexp default is anchored (or replaced with exact --certificate-identity match), and the script hard-fails (non-zero exit) when the parsed artifact list from checksums-sha256.txt is empty or below an expected minimum count, verified by a manual run against a release with an intentionally truncated checksums file.

title: Add CF Access as OIDC provider: unified identity → bridge cert flow
description:
CF Access can act as a generic OIDC provider (SaaS app mode). Signet already has a pluggable provider registry. Adding CF Access as a provider means:

1. CF Access authenticates user (Google, GitHub, Okta, OTP — whatever methods configured)
2. CF Access issues OIDC JWT
3. Signet validates JWT (CF Access = another provider alongside GitHub Actions, Clerk)
4. Signet mints bridge cert binding user's key to CF Access-verified identity

Two birds: CF Access handles login UX + session management, signet handles crypto + cert issuance. No redundant auth layers.

Config addition to authority.json:
```json
{"name": "cf-access", "issuer": "https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs"}
```

CF Access free tier: 50 users, includes OIDC. No additional cost.

This is a signet change (provider config), not rig. The provider registry code already handles generic OIDC — just needs CF Access JWKS endpoint configured.

Ref: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/http-apps/saas-apps/generic-oidc-saas/

Relates to: rig auth-chain thread, rig-959350 (signet-at-edge)
